lines.text: Mmm… Oh no! This cake is terrible!
What? Let me try.
Yuck! It is not sweet at all!
Finn, what did you put in the cake?
The sugar, Dad. From the white box.
The white box? That is the salt!
Mom is coming home at twelve. What can we do?
Don't worry. Let's make something else.
Let's use fruit! We have apples and bananas.
And ice cream!
Let's put the fruit on the ice cream.
Good idea, Ruby! Can you cut the bananas?
OK! Finn, you wash the apples.
OK. But let's not use the white box!
Mom! What's the weather like?
Look out of the window. It's raining.
But the phone said, "It's going to be sunny!"
I know. The phone was wrong.
So no picnic by the river?
Not today. It's cold and wet outside.
Mom! Is it raining? No picnic?
Wait, Toby. I have an idea.
Let's have a picnic here, on the floor!
Here? In the living room?
Yes! A big green blanket is our grass.
And the sandwiches?
They're ready! Come and eat.
A picnic in the rain. I love it!
Hello! I have my new library card.
Hello, Amir! What can I do for you?
I want these books, please.
That's twelve books!
How many books can I borrow?
Five books at one time.
Only five? Oh.
How long can I keep them?
For two weeks.
When do I bring them back?
On Saturday, June 20. It's on your card.
What happens if I'm late?
You must pay a little money. So don't be late!
I won't. And then I can take five more!
Mrs. Kerr, can I ask a question?
Of course, Noah.
Can I take Bubbles home for the holiday?
Hmm. Can you feed him every day?
Yes, two times a day!
And can you clean the water on Saturday?
Yes, I can. My mom can help me.
OK. Yes, you can take him.
Thank you! May I take his food, too?
Yes. Here you are. Not too much!
Can I take the fishbowl to my bedroom?
Your bedroom? Why?
We have a cat. His name is Tiger.
Oh! Then yes, you can. Close the door!
Zoe, I want a photo of Bella.
OK, Grandpa. First, touch the camera here.
This one? The little black camera?
Yes! Then look at the screen.
I can see Bella! She is on the sofa.
Good. Now press the big white circle.
Like this?
Yes! Now you have a photo.
Wonderful! How do I send it to the family?
Touch the photo, then touch "Send."
Send, send, send…
Grandpa, stop! Don't press it again!
Oh. How many photos did I send?
Twenty, Grandpa. Twenty photos of Bella!
Good morning! What can I get you?
Good morning, dear. Can I have a tea, please?
A tea. Would you like milk?
Yes, please. And no sugar.
Tea with milk, no sugar. OK.
Are you writing it down?
Yes. It's my first day.
And I make a lot of mistakes.
Everyone has a first day. Take your time.
Thank you. Anything else?
Can I have a piece of lemon cake, please?
Lemon cake… not chocolate cake. Right!
That's six dollars, please.
Here you are. And well done, dear.
Hiro? Is that you?
Alice! Hello!
Hello! Welcome to New York!
Thank you! Arigato!
How was your flight?
It was OK. But it was very long.
Was it long? How many hours?
Thirteen hours!
Wow! Are you tired?
Yes, a little. I didn't sleep much.
Are you hungry? My mom has pizza at home.
Hello, Alice. Hiro talks about you every day!
Mom!
Nice to meet you, Mrs. Tanaka!
Let's go home and eat!
Hi, kids! What are you doing?
We're making a robot, Dad!
A robot? From boxes?
Yes! I'm painting its eyes.
It looks great. Is it for school?
Yes, for the science fair on Friday.
So why are you sad, Omar?
There is a problem. It isn't moving.
We're pushing it, but it's just a box.
Hmm. A robot has to move.
Wait here. I'm getting something from the house.
What are you getting, Dad?
Your old toy car. It has a small motor!
A motor! Now it can move!
Hello, Mei. I'm Dr. Adams. What's wrong?
My arm hurts.
I see. What happened?
I fell from a tree in the park.
She was very high in the tree.
OK. Can you move your hand?
Yes, a little.
Does it hurt here?
No, not much.
And here?
Yes! It hurts a lot!
Let's take an x-ray. Maybe it's broken.
Don't worry, Mei. I'm here.
Hello. I saw your poster. I'm looking for my dog.
Hello. What does your dog look like?
It's small. It's brown and white.
Does it have a collar?
Yes, it has a red collar.
Hmm. And its ears? Are they big?
Yes, very big! And one ear is white.
One white ear… Just a moment.
Is this your dog?
Biscuit! Oh, it's you!
His name is Biscuit? I called him Rainy.
Rainy is a good name, too. Thank you so much.
He is a very good dog.
Then come and walk him on Saturday!
I'm so sorry. It was my goal.
Sophie! Don't worry.
But the ball was between my hands!
It was a very hard kick.
The tall boy is very good.
And you are very good, too. We need you!
Amara is right, Sophie.
Coach, I'm afraid.
That's OK. Forget the goal.
Watch the ball, not the boy.
Watch the ball… not the boy.
Yes! You can do it, Sophie!
Now go. Good luck!
Thanks. I can do it!
Grandma! It's so hot in here!
Is it? I'm OK. I'm just a little tired.
Mom, your face is very red.
And you're wearing a sweater!
I like this sweater.
You shouldn't wear it today, Grandma.
And you should drink some water.
But I'm not thirsty.
Old people often don't feel thirsty. But you need water.
OK, OK. You're right.
Why don't you come to the library with us?
The library? Why?
It's cool there. You should read the newspaper with me.
A cool library and my granddaughter? That sounds good.
Hi! Can I sit here?
Yes.
I'm Emily. What's your name?
I'm Nora.
Nice to meet you, Nora. Where are you from?
I'm from Brazil.
Brazil! Wow. Is this your notebook?
Yes. I like to draw.
Your pictures are beautiful! Is this a cat?
Yes. In Portuguese, "gato."
Gato! Can I draw a cat, too?
OK! Nice to meet you, Emily.
Grandpa, look at this old photo!
Oh! Where was it?
In your desk. Who is the young man?
That was me! I was twenty.
You were young! And where was this?
This was Park Street, sixty years ago.
Were there big shops?
No. There were small shops, and there was a cinema.
Was it a good cinema?
It was the best! I was there every Saturday.
Every Saturday? Why?
Your grandma was there, too.
Grandpa! Is the cinema still there?
I don't know. Let's go and see!
Daniel, look at this poster. A singing contest!
So?
You can sing. You can really sing!
At home, yes. In my room.
Can you sing in the contest?
No! I can't sing in front of people.
Why not?
My face goes red, and my legs shake.
I understand. But I can help you.
How?
First, sing for me.
Then for Mom and Dad. Then for Grandma.
And then for the school?
Yes! You can do it.
OK… I can try.
Hello, Mr. Grant! Are you OK?
Hello, Hana. I can't open my door.
Wow, that's a lot of snow!
Can we help you? We have Dad's shovel.
Oh, thank you. Yes, please!
I can help, too. I have a small shovel.
You are very kind children.
Do you need anything from the shop?
Hmm. Some milk and some bread, please.
We can go now!
Wait! First the door, then the shop.
OK! And our snowman can help, too.
Theo! My tooth is moving!
Let me see. Oh, it's wobbly!
Is it going to hurt?
How do you feel, Poppy?
I'm scared.
Don't be scared. It doesn't hurt much.
Are you sure?
Yes. I had eight wobbly teeth!
Eight? Were you scared?
A little. But then the tooth fairy came.
The tooth fairy? Who is that?
She takes your tooth, and she gives you a gift.
A gift? Now I'm not scared. I'm excited!
Good! Now eat your breakfast.
Excuse me. Where is this?
This is Airport Road.
Airport Road? Oh no!
Are you OK? Where do you want to go?
The park in the city. I took the wrong bus.
Don't worry. Wait here for the number 5.
Does the number 5 go to the park?
Yes, it does. It stops near the park.
Thank you very much!
You're welcome. Call your mom, OK?
Leo? Where are you?
Mom, I'm OK! I'm near the airport.
The airport? Oh, Leo!
Don't worry, Mom. The number 5 is coming!
Hello, Rossi's Pizza!
Hi! Can I order some pizzas for a school party?
Yes, of course. How many pizzas?
Twenty, please.
Twenty? Wow! Just a moment.
Dad, how much are twenty pizzas?
Ten dollars for one. So, two hundred dollars.
It's two hundred dollars. Is that OK?
Yes, that's fine.
What time do you need them?
At six o'clock, please.
Six o'clock. OK! And the address?
The school near the river. Thank you!
Twenty pizzas at six? It's three o'clock now!
Oh no! What happened?
The red tomatoes are not here!
Ava! What happened?
Look at our plants!
Who ate our tomatoes?
I don't know.
I know! The big boys from Class 5A!
Wait, Lucas. We don't know that.
Look at the ground. What can you see?
Very small footprints!
They are not big boys' feet.
Right. So who ate them?
Something small… and hungry!
Chloe, I've decided something. I'm going to run a marathon.
A marathon? Dad, have you ever run a marathon?
No, I've never run a marathon. That's why it's a challenge!
Have you ever run ten kilometers?
Hmm… no. I've run five kilometers. Once.
Dad! A marathon is forty-two kilometers!
I know. I've already made a training plan.
Have you bought running shoes?
Not yet. But I've found a good shop.
What about your diet? You love burgers.
I've never eaten so much salad in my life!
Have you ever injured your legs?
Never. My legs are strong.
OK. I'll come with you on my bike and check your speed.
That's the best idea I've ever heard!
OK, we have the lemon juice. What do we do first?
First, mix the butter and the sugar.
How long?
Until it's soft and pale. Grandma always said that.
Done. Then what?
After that, add the eggs, the flour and the cinnamon.
And the lemon juice?
Yes! Three spoons. Not two, not four.
Three spoons… with love.
Then pour the mix into the pan.
Do the plums go inside?
No, on top. Aunt Lucia remembered that.
Finally, we bake it. For how long?
Forty minutes. And this time, we watch the oven!
No more burned cakes!
Terrible weather, isn't it?
Yes, it is. I've never seen so much snow.
Three hours, the driver said. Where are you going?
Home, to my parents. It's my first visit since September.
How lovely. Are you a student?
Yes, I'm at college in the city.
And what do you study?
Music. That's my cello. How about you? Are you visiting family?
Yes, my grandchildren. They're five and seven.
I like your scarf. It's a lovely color.
Thank you! My granddaughter made it.
So, do you play in concerts?
Not really. I get very nervous in front of an audience.
Nervous? That's normal. Everybody is.
Maybe. By the way, I'm Theo.
Nice to meet you, Theo. I'm Ada.
Nice to meet you, too.
Marcus can't sing on Saturday. His voice is gone.
So we have to cancel.
No. Leo, you can sing!
Me? No way. I play the drums.
But you wrote the songs. You know every word.
Writing is different. I'd be terrible.
Why not try? You'd be great!
There will be a thousand people in the audience!
Come on, Leo. Just try one song. Only for us.
I'm too nervous.
Everyone is nervous before a festival.
What have you got to lose?
My friends… if I sing badly!
Ha! We'll still be your friends. Come on!
OK. One song. Where's the microphone?
Right here. Let's practice!
Good morning. I'm afraid there's a problem with my bike.
Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. What happened?
Your assistant repaired the brakes on Friday.
On Saturday, they didn't work, and I fell at a traffic light.
Oh no! Are you OK?
My arm hurts, but I'll live.
Let me have a look at the bike.
Hmm. This brake is loose. That's dangerous.
Mr. Grant… it was my fault.
There were a lot of customers, and I didn't check it twice.
Well… at least you're honest.
We'll repair it right now, and you don't have to pay.
And I'll test it three times on the street.
Thank you. That's all I wanted.
Please take this new helmet, too. It's a gift.
Now that's good customer service!
OK, Dev. Tell me what happened.
Someone stole my new bike outside the bookshop.
What time was it?
About half past ten this morning.
And what were you doing at that time?
I was looking at comics inside the shop.
Was anyone standing near your bike?
Yes. A man was waiting across the street.
What was he wearing?
He was wearing a grey hoodie and black jeans.
What was he doing?
He was talking on his phone and watching the shop.
Good. That's very helpful. Can you describe your bike?
It's blue, and there's a lion sticker under the seat.
A lion? That's a very good detail. We'll do our best, Dev.
Mason, are you free next weekend?
I think so. Why?
Shall we go camping? Just you and me.
Camping? Where?
How about Pine Lake? It's in the middle of a forest.
Is there Wi-Fi?
No Wi-Fi, no phones, no TV. Just nature.
That sounds a bit boring, Dad.
Boring? We can swim, go hiking and cook by the lake!
OK… What shall we take?
A tent, two sleeping bags, food and a map.
And my old compass. Your grandpa gave it to me.
What about the weather?
I checked. It's going to be sunny all weekend.
Shall we pack a raincoat, just in case?
A raincoat? You worry too much!
So, Detective Ivy, who is the thief?
I don't know yet. But I have some clues.
Look. There are crumbs next to the jar.
Maybe it was Grandpa. He wakes up at night.
It can't be Grandpa. He doesn't like chocolate.
Then it might be Dad. He's on a diet.
It might be Dad… People on a diet are always hungry.
Or it might be you, Detective!
Very funny. I was asleep.
What about Pepper?
It can't be Pepper. The jar is too high for a dog.
So the thief must be tall.
Yes. It must be someone tall… like you!
Me? I'm innocent!
We'll see. Tonight, I'm going to watch the kitchen.
I saw your advertisement in my mailbox. This is Biscuit.
Hello, Biscuit! Oh, he's so sweet.
How often does he go out?
Twice a day. At eight in the morning and at five.
And how long is each walk?
Usually about half an hour. He's quite slow.
Does he ever run?
Hardly ever. Only when he sees a cat.
Does he like cats?
No! He's afraid of them. He runs away.
Oh dear. How often does he eat?
Every morning and every evening. And he gets one biscuit on Sundays.
Only once a week? Poor Biscuit!
He's a big boy. He needs to be careful.
Don't worry. I'll put all his walks in my calendar.
So, Lucas, how was your first week?
Great! But everything is different here.
Different how?
Well, your school is much bigger than mine.
You even have a stadium!
Yeah, football is the most important sport here.
And dinner is much earlier. In France, we eat at eight.
Eight? I'd be so hungry!
The portions are bigger here, too. The biggest pizza I've ever seen!
Is French food better than American food?
Hmm… it's not as big, but it's… more interesting.
That's very polite! What about people?
People here are friendlier with strangers. They talk to me in shops!
And in France?
In France, we're quieter. But we kiss more!
I know! My face was redder than a tomato at the airport!
Yes! A new phone! Just a small fee…
Ana, what are you doing with Mom's card?
I won a prize! Look at this message.
Stop! Don't type anything!
Why not? It's only two dollars.
Be careful. This is a scam.
How do you know?
Look at the address. It's really strange.
And there are mistakes in the English.
But the website has a photo of the phone.
Anyone can put a photo on a website. It's an old trick.
If you type Mom's card number, they'll take all the money in her account.
All the money? Oh no…
Watch out for messages like this. Never click the link.
I clicked it already. Is that a problem?
Close it now, delete the message, and let's tell Mom.
OK. Thanks, Leo. That was close!
Maya? Can I come in?
Go away.
Please. I want to apologize.
You promised to help me. I waited the whole afternoon.
I know. I'm really sorry, Maya.
It was my fault. I shouldn't have gone to Jake's house.
You forgot about me.
Yes, I forgot. And that's not OK.
Why should I trust you now?
Can I make it up to you?
Tomorrow we can build the volcano. The whole day.
The whole day? No games?
No games, no phone. You can keep my phone until Monday.
Promise?
I promise. This time I really mean it.
OK. But I'm keeping your phone!
Hello, Noor. Thank you for coming. Look at this image.
Is that the painting of the valley?
Yes. It's an x-ray. It shows the layers under the paint.
Sorry, what does "layers" mean?
Layers are like floors in a building. One on top of another.
So you mean there's another painting under the landscape?
Exactly. A portrait of a young woman.
The painter reused the canvas in the eighteenth century.
Sorry, could you say that again, please?
Of course. He painted on the same canvas two times.
Why? What do you mean?
Paint and canvas were very expensive then.
So you mean he painted over his first picture to save money?
Maybe. Or maybe he didn't like it.
And now, after three hundred years, we can see her again.
Thanks to you, Noor. You really looked.
Zoe, it's getting dark.
I know. The ghost comes after five, remember?
Half the class is too frightened to come here now.
Good. I love a mystery.
Are you scared of ghosts?
No. Ghosts don't exist. I'm not scared of ghosts.
Then what are you afraid of?
Hmm… I'm afraid of spiders. And exams!
Exams? Don't be silly!
What about you? Are you scared of ghosts?
Not really. But I'm scared of the dark.
The dark? Why?
When I was small, I saw a big shadow in my room. I screamed.
What was it?
My coat on the door.
Ha! You're braver than you think.
Wait… did you hear that?
Something's moving in there! I'm not scared. I'm just… very careful.
I'm sorry, Lena. I think it's time to close the shop.
Close? No! We can't win on price.
But we can offer something different.
Like what?
Your knowledge, Grandma. You know everything about flowers.
How about a weekend workshop? You could teach people to make bouquets.
A workshop? I'm not sure. I'm not a teacher.
But you talk to customers every day. That's teaching!
Hmm. That's a good idea, but who will come?
What if we put photos of your flowers online every day?
Online? At my age?
I'll do that part. And we could deliver flowers by bike.
Deliver? To whom?
Old people in the area. They can't always come to the shop.
That's a good idea. Mrs. Brown can't walk far anymore.
So… how about we try for three months?
Three months. OK. If it fails, I'll pay the rent with your photos!
Good afternoon. How can I help you?
Hi. My suitcase is missing. It wasn't on the belt.
I'm sorry to hear that. Which flight were you on?
The flight from Paris. It arrived an hour ago.
Did you change planes in Paris?
Yes. There was a delay, and I almost missed my second flight.
That's probably the reason. Bags sometimes stay behind.
But I've lost something really important.
Don't worry. Can you describe your suitcase?
It's large and green, with a black handle and four wheels.
Large, green, black handle… Is there a label?
Yes, a red label with my name on it. Rana Costa.
What's inside? Anything expensive?
A wedding dress. My cousin's wedding is on Saturday!
OK. Here's your form and your number.
We'll call you as soon as we find it.
Thank you. Please find it before Saturday!
So, which plants will grow faster?
I think the classical music plants will win.
No way. I bet the rap plants will win.
Why?
Rap is full of energy. They'll probably dance!
Kofi, plants don't have ears.
OK. What about the quiet plants?
I don't think they'll grow very much.
How tall will they be in six weeks?
Maybe twenty centimeters. Maybe a bit more.
And mine will be thirty. I'm sure.
We'll see. Don't forget, the test has to be fair.
I know. Same light, same water, same boxes.
And we write down every result, even the bad ones.
There won't be any bad ones. My plants will be stars.
I hope you're right. But I don't think you are.
Tariq! How's Northgate?
Grey. It rains every day.
And your new school?
It's OK. The students are polite.
But?
But I don't know a single person. I sit alone at lunch.
That sounds lonely.
I miss home. I miss our team. I miss you, too.
I miss you, too. The team isn't the same without you.
I'm worried that nobody here will ever talk to me.
It's hard to start again. But it'll get better.
How do you know?
Is there a football team at your school?
I think so. Training is on Thursdays.
Then go! That's how you met me, remember?
You're right. OK, I'll go on Thursday.
I'm sure you'll score. Tell me everything!
Hello? Can anybody hear me? I'm stuck in here!
Hello! Yes, I'm here. My name's Jamal. Are you OK?
I'm Mrs. Weiss, from the eighth floor. It's very dark in here.
Don't worry. I'll call the emergency number now.
Thank you, dear. I'm a bit frightened.
They're sending an engineer. But it might take two hours.
Two hours!
I'll stay here with you. Do you need anything?
Is everything all right? I heard voices.
Mrs. Weiss is stuck in the elevator.
Oh no. I'll get some candles from my apartment.
Mrs. Weiss, would you like some hot tea?
Yes, please! And do you have a blanket? It's cold.
My sister has one. I'll bring it now.
You're very kind. I've never met my neighbors before.
Well, now you have!
Welcome back to Radio Hill! Our guest isn't here.
So today, we have a question for you.
What do you think about school lunches?
Come to the radio room and tell us!
Hi! Can I say something?
Of course! What's your name, and what do you think?
I'm Jade. In my opinion, the pizza is great.
But I think the soup is awful.
Awful? Why?
It has no taste. It's like hot water!
I disagree. I think the soup is fine.
Interesting! Why do you disagree?
It's healthy. It just needs more salt.
So you agree that it has no taste?
Well… yes, I agree about that!
What a lively discussion! What do you think, listeners?
Yara, look! There's a shark in the river!
Really? Where did you see that?
Online. Everyone's sharing this photo.
Hmm. Who took it?
I don't know. Does it matter?
Of course it matters. How do we know it's real?
Because thousands of people have shared it!
That doesn't make it true. It might be fake.
But it looks so real. Look at that fin!
Can sharks even live in rivers?
I'm not sure. Maybe some can?
Let's ask an expert before we write anything.
OK. And let's check where the photo came from.
Good idea. If it's fake, that's our story.
A story about a shark that isn't there?
Exactly. But first, the facts.
Excuse me. Could you help me, please?
Of course. Are you lost?
A little. I'm looking for the Sleeping Lion.
Ah, the stone lion! It's not far from here.
Great! How do I get there?
Go straight on until you get to the roundabout.
Straight on to the roundabout. OK.
Then turn left and walk past the bank.
Sorry, did you say left or right?
Left. The lion is opposite the bookshop. You can't miss it.
How far is it? Can I walk?
Yes, it's about ten minutes on foot.
Thank you so much. You've been very helpful.
You're welcome. Although… I haven't seen that lion for years.
Shh! Is Nana asleep?
Yes. I can hear her in her room.
Good. OK, we need to plan the party.
Who's going to invite the guests?
I'll do that. I've got all her friends' numbers.
And who's going to buy the balloons?
You are. And you can make the sign, too.
OK. I'll buy forty balloons!
Forty? Where are you going to hide them?
Under my bed. Nana never looks there.
Fine. Mom and Dad are going to take her to the cinema.
What if she doesn't want to go?
She loves films. She'll go.
What if she finds out?
She won't. But don't forget: not a word to anyone at school!
I promise. I'm very good at secrets.
Hello? Is that Bell's Bakery?
Yes, it is. How can I help you?
Can I speak to Nora Bell, please?
Speaking. Who's calling, please?
It's Martin Hughes, from Hill Farm. My daughter's getting married!
Oh, congratulations! When is the wedding?
On Saturday. It's small and very romantic.
Sorry, you're breaking up. Could you say that again?
Saturday! The cake is for thirty people.
For… how many people? I can't hear you very well.
And we can pay about three hundred dollars.
Three hundred? Wow! That's a very big cake!
Sorry? What did you say?
I said, no problem! I'll start today!
Hello? Hello? Are you still there?
The line's terrible. I'll call you back!
OK, candidate Nadia. Why should I vote for you?
Because I listen. I asked everybody about our school.
Louder, please! I can't hear you at the back.
Because I listen!
Better. So, what will you do if you win?
If I win, I'll ask for a quiet room in the library.
Marcus says he'll give us pizza every week.
I won't promise pizza. I can't pay for it!
Ha! Fair. What else?
If you vote for me, I'll ask the school to fix the lockers.
And the new students? They don't know anyone.
I'll start a lunch club for them. I promise.
What will you do if you lose?
If I lose, I'll start the club anyway.
Then I'll vote for you. And I'll tell everybody.
Ow! My ankle! I think I've broken it!
Tom, stay calm. Don't move. Let me have a look.
It really hurts, Nadia.
I know. Can you move your toes?
Yes… a little.
Good. That's a good sign. Does it hurt when I touch here?
Yes! Don't touch it!
Sorry. OK, you're injured, but you're going to be OK.
How can we get down? I can't walk in this fog.
We're not going down. It's too dangerous. We'll wait here, behind this rock.
I'm so cold. I can't stop shaking.
Put my jacket on. Try to keep your hands inside. We need to keep you warm.
Did you call for help?
Yes. The rescue team knows where we are. Help is on the way.
How long will it take?
A few hours, maybe. But they'll find us. I promise.
I feel so tired. I just want to sleep.
No, Tom. You need to stay awake. Keep talking to me. Tell me about your holiday plans.
My holiday? Somewhere warm. Definitely somewhere warm.
Good morning, Richard. How are you getting on?
Much better, thank you. I feel like a different person.
Your blood pressure has come down a lot. What have you changed?
Well, I've started walking to work. It takes forty minutes.

Please do. I confess I was surprised you sent them to us at all.
The parchment appears to come from the tenth century. That creates a genuine discrepancy with my original argument.
Priya shared the report within an hour of opening it, Anders. I thought you should know that.
Admirable. But a gap of a century is hardly a detail. How do you account for it?
The evidence would seem to suggest that the book is a copy. The archaic features may belong to an older exemplar.
May belong. You were far more confident in chapter three.
I was, and I overstated it. At this stage it would be premature to offer more than a plausible hypothesis.
A hypothesis you can substantiate, or merely a conjecture?
Partly both. The spellings fit eighth-century models, but I'm not in a position to date the exemplar precisely.
And the calibration curve? Some colleagues would call it unreliable for that period.
Some would, but I'd be cautious about hiding behind that. The simplest reading of the dates is probably the correct one.
If I may, that is exactly the kind of caution we hope to see in a young scholar.
Let's test it, then. Why is this abbreviation archaic rather than simply old-fashioned?
To the best of my knowledge, it vanishes from Scottish books after about 800. But I admit the sample is small.
How small, exactly?
Eleven examples. Enough to suggest a pattern, but not enough to prove one.
And line forty-two? You treat it as a correction by a second hand.
One plausible interpretation is that, yes. But the damage allows both readings, and I've tried to show that uncertainty in a footnote.
So you have. I missed it entirely.
Shall we pause there? I think we've covered the essential points.
We have. Ms Raman, would you mind waiting outside while we talk it over?
Of course. Whatever you decide, thank you for taking the argument so seriously.
I nearly didn't come. I sat in the car park for ten minutes.
I'm really glad you did. There's no rush. Can I get you a tea first?
Tea's fine. But nobody can know I've talked to you.
Your anonymity comes first. I won't name you, and I won't publish anything that could identify you without asking.
All right. Where do you want me to start?
Wherever feels easiest. How long have you worked at Beechwood?
Nine years. I love the residents. Most of them are very frail now.
You mentioned a lady who died in March. Could you say a little more about that?
Mrs Lindqvist. She taught me chess. She went into hospital with dehydration and never came back.
I'm so sorry. What happened in the days before she was admitted?
There were two of us for forty-six people at night. We couldn't get round everyone with drinks.
When you say you couldn't get round, what do you mean exactly?
Some people didn't get a drink for hours. Sometimes all night.
And the fluid charts? Your message said something about them.
We were told to fill them in anyway. As if the drinks had been given.
Just to be clear, the manager told you directly to record drinks that weren't given?
In a meeting, in front of four of us. I did it. That's the part I can't live with.
How did that make you feel, at the time?
Sick. And scared. If I refused, I'd lose my job, and the residents would have one carer fewer.
That's an impossible position. I'll need to substantiate all this before anything is published, you understand.
I took photos of the rotas. And the hospital will have her real records.
If their notes and the home's charts don't match, that discrepancy will speak for itself.
And if they find out it was me?
There's legal protection against retaliation, and I'll put you in touch with a lawyer. Is there anything I haven't asked that I should have?
Yes. Ask me why it took me six months to call you. I'll tell you next time.
You came all the way from Aberdeen. You must want something.
I suppose I do. There's something I've wanted to say for thirty years, and I'm running out of excuses.
Go on, then.
What I said at Dad's funeral was cruel and untrue. I was wrong to say it, and I've regretted it every single day.
You said I was never part of the family.
I know. I'm not asking you to forgive me. I just didn't want you to go on thinking I meant it.
For thirty years I assumed you did. Every Christmas without a card felt like a reproach.
For me it was the same. I thought your silence was a verdict on me.
We were both so proud. It became irrevocable without either of us deciding anything.
I should have asked why you couldn't come home that year. I just assumed you didn't care.
I was going through a divorce. And I lost a baby that spring. I never told anyone.
Kitty, I had no idea. I'm so sorry. You were carrying all that on your own?
I didn't want to add to your burdens. You were already nursing Dad.
So we each had a grievance, and each of us hid half the story.
That sounds like our family, doesn't it? Dad never explained anything either.
Remember his Sunday dinners? He explained those at great length.
The potatoes he set on fire. I'd forgotten about that.
You look frail, Kitty. Is it very hard, the dialysis?
Three times a week, four hours each time. I'm tired all the time.
Could we try to see each other more often? Whatever happens with your health.
I'd like that. I'm not sure it's a reconciliation yet, but it's a beginning.
A beginning is more than I dared hope for on the train.
More tea, then? Dad would say we've been estranged long enough.

paras: It is Monday morning, and it is raining.
The sky is dark and gray.
In the city, people walk fast under their umbrellas.
The buses are full, and the taxis are busy.
There is water on the streets, so the cars go slowly.
A little boy jumps in the water and laughs.
His mother is not happy, because his shoes are full of water.
In the park, the trees and flowers drink the rain.
The cafes are warm, and they smell of coffee.
Many people stop there and wait.
At twelve o'clock, the rain stops.
The sun comes out, and the city is bright again.
Welcome to the Green Hill School Library!
The library is open from Monday to Friday, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
On Saturday, it is open in the morning.
It is closed on Sunday.
Please read these rules.
Be quiet in the reading room.
Do not eat or drink near the books.
You can borrow three books for two weeks.
Please bring your student card.
If your book is late, you must pay one dollar a day.
Do you need help?
Ask Ms. Brown at the front desk.
She is happy to help you find a good book.
This is Anna.
She is eleven years old, and she lives in a small town near the sea.
Anna has a big family.
Her father is a doctor at the town hospital.
Her mother is a teacher, and she teaches music.
Anna has two brothers.
Tom is sixteen, and he loves football.
Ben is only five.
He likes cartoons and chocolate.
Anna's grandmother lives with them too.
She makes a cake every Sunday.
On Sunday evening, the family eats dinner together and talks about the week.
Anna thinks it is the best time of the week.
In the morning, people around the world eat very different food.
In the United States, many people eat eggs and bread with butter.
In Japan, breakfast can be rice, soup and fish.
In Vietnam, a lot of people eat a hot bowl of pho.
Pho is a soup with beef or chicken.
In Mexico, people often eat eggs with beans.
In England, a big breakfast has eggs, meat, beans, tomatoes and bread.
In France, breakfast is small: bread, butter and a cup of coffee.
Some people drink tea, and some drink juice.
Doctors say that breakfast is an important meal.
It helps us feel good and think well at school or at work.
What do you eat for breakfast?
Hi Sam!
I am at work, and I am going to be late today.
Please take the bus home after school.
The key is under the small box near the door.
There is some soup in the kitchen.
You can have it with bread.
Please feed the cat, too.
Her food is on the top shelf.
Do your homework before you watch TV!
Grandma is going to call you at six.
I will be home at eight o'clock.
Call me if you have a problem.
Love, Mom
The tiger is the biggest cat in the world.
It is orange, with black lines on its body.
Tigers live in Asia, often near rivers.
A tiger can be as long as a small car.
It is very strong, and it can run fast.
Tigers can swim, and they like water.
Most cats do not like water, so this is special.
A tiger usually lives alone.
It sleeps in the day and looks for food at night.
Baby tigers stay with their mother for about two years.
Today, there are not many tigers in the world.
Many people work hard to save them.
Everybody needs sleep.
When we sleep, our body and our brain get ready for a new day.
Children need a lot of sleep: about ten hours every night.
Their parents need seven or eight hours.
Some people go to bed late and wake up early.
Then they feel tired all day.
It is hard to think and learn when you are tired.
Here are some easy ideas for good sleep.
Go to bed at the same time every night.
Do not drink coffee or coke in the evening.
Turn off your phone and the TV one hour before bed.
Read a book or listen to quiet music.
Keep your bedroom dark and cool.
Good night, and sleep well!
Mr. Green is a farmer.
He wakes up at five o'clock every morning.
First, he feeds the cows and the pigs.
Then he gets the eggs from the chickens.
His wife makes breakfast, and they eat together in the kitchen.
After breakfast, Mr. Green drives his old truck to the field.
He grows corn, potatoes and tomatoes.
The work is hard, and the sun is hot.
At twelve, he sits under a big tree and has lunch.
In the afternoon, he sells vegetables to a shop in town.
People love his tomatoes because they are red and sweet.
In the evening, Mr. Green is very tired, but he is happy.
He goes to bed at nine o'clock.
Come to Sunny Cup, the new café on Park Street!
We are open every day from 7 a.m. to 9 p.m.
We have hot drinks and cold drinks.
Try our coffee with milk, our green tea or our orange juice.
For breakfast, there are eggs, bread and yogurt with fruit.
For lunch, we make sandwiches, salads and soup.
Our chocolate cake is famous in the town!
The café has free Wi-Fi, big tables and a quiet corner for reading.
Students get a special price on Monday.
Bring a friend, and your second coffee is free.
See you soon!
There are about 7,000 languages in the world.
Every language has a word for hello.
In Spanish, people say "hola."
In French, they say "bonjour."
In Vietnamese, you can say "xin chào."
In Japanese, people often say "konnichiwa" in the afternoon.
People do not only use words when they meet.
In Thailand, people put their hands together.
In many English places, people shake hands.
In France, friends often kiss each other two times.
Learning to say hello is a great first step in a new language.
Can you say hello in three languages?
I have an old blue bike.
It was my father's bike when he was young.
It is not beautiful, and the bell is broken.
But I love it.
I ride it to school every day.
It takes fifteen minutes.
On the way, I see the river, a big bridge and a small church.
On Saturday, I ride with my friends to the hill.
We eat sandwiches there and play games.
Last month, a wheel of my bike was broken.
My father and I worked on it together, and now it is fine.
My father says the bike is older than me, but it is still strong.
Hi Lucy,
How are you?
I have some good news.
My family and I are coming to your town this weekend!
We are going to stay at a hotel near the beach.
We arrive on Saturday morning.
Are you free on Saturday afternoon?
We can go to the beach or see a movie.
In the evening, my parents want to have dinner at a fish restaurant.
You and your mom can come too!
On Sunday, we leave at four o'clock.
Please write back soon.
See you on Saturday!
Emma
Class 4B: Our Week
Monday: math in the morning and English in the afternoon.
Tuesday: science with Mr. Hill.
Please bring your notebook and a pencil.
Wednesday: history and art.
On Wednesday, we paint in the art room, so wear old clothes!
Thursday: music and a grammar test.
Friday: sports and a class meeting.
Lunch is at twelve o'clock every day.
School finishes at three thirty.
Do your homework every evening, and read for twenty minutes.
If you have a question, ask your teacher, Ms. Wood.
What do you wear today?
That changes with the weather.
In spring, the weather is often warm, but it can be rainy.
Take a light jacket and an umbrella.
In summer, it is hot and sunny.
Wear a T-shirt, shorts and a cap, and drink a lot of water.
In autumn, it is cool, there is a lot of wind, and the leaves are yellow and red.
Jeans and a warm shirt are good for autumn.
In winter, it is cold, and in some places it is snowy.
You need a thick coat, a hat and warm shoes.
On a foggy morning, wear bright colors.
Then drivers can see you on the street.
Your body is like a wonderful machine.
Your heart works all day and all night.
It never stops, even when you sleep.
Your brain is in your head, and it helps you think, remember and dream.
You see with your eyes, and you hear with your ears.
You smell with your nose.
You eat and speak with your mouth.
Most grown men and women have 32 teeth.
There are more than 200 bones in your body.
Your arms, legs, knees and shoulders can move because of these bones.
Every minute, you breathe about fifteen times.
Take care of your body: eat well, sleep well and move every day.
Please come to Mia's birthday party!
Mia is going to be eight years old.
Date: Saturday, June 14
Time: from two o'clock to five o'clock
Address: 12 Rose Street, near the park
There is going to be cake, ice cream and fruit juice.
We are going to play games and dance to music in the garden.
Please wear something pink or purple.
Mia loves pink more than any other color!
You do not need to bring a gift.
Just bring a smile.
Can you come?
Please call Mia's dad before Wednesday.
On Friday, it was Sports Day at Lake View School.
The weather was sunny and warm.
All the students were in four teams: red, blue, green and yellow.
In the morning, there were running and jumping games.
The little children had a fun game with eggs.
In the afternoon, the older students played soccer, basketball and volleyball.
Sara from the blue team kicked the ball into the goal three times!
Many parents came to watch.
They called out the names of their children.
At the end of the day, the green team won the gold cup.
But the coach, Mr. Brown, said, "Everyone is a winner today!"
On a night with no clouds, look up at the sky.
You can see the moon and many stars.
The stars look very small, but many of them are bigger than our sun.
They look small because they are very, very far away.
The moon does not make its own light.
The light of the sun gets to the moon, and we see it.
The moon looks different every night.
On some nights it is a big circle.
On other nights it is a thin line.
In the city, it is hard to see the stars.
There are too many lights on the streets and in the buildings.
In the mountains or on a small island, the sky is dark.
There, you can see so many stars.
Every month has a special day.
The year starts with New Year on January 1.
People stay awake until twelve o'clock and watch fireworks.
In February, there is Valentine's Day, a day for love.
In March or April, many families celebrate Easter with eggs and chocolate.
Summer is the time for holidays and trips to the beach.
On October 31, children wear ghost and monster clothes for Halloween.
In November, American families eat a big turkey dinner for Thanksgiving.
In December, there is Christmas.
People put lights on trees and give gifts.
They say "Merry Christmas!" to each other.
What is your favorite festival?
Cats and dogs are the two most loved pets in the world.
But they are very different.
A dog needs a lot of time.
You have to walk it every day, and it likes to play with you.
Dogs are happy in a group, and they love their owners very much.
When you come home, your dog runs to the door.
A cat is different.
It sleeps for about fifteen hours a day!
It keeps its body clean, and it does not need a walk.
A cat likes you, but it wants some time alone.
So, are you a cat person or a dog person?
Some people love both!
Welcome to the City Zoo!
We are open every day from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.
Tickets: 12 dollars, or 6 dollars for children.
Walk along the green line to see the lions and the tigers.
The blue line goes to the monkeys and the birds.
The snake house is behind the café.
At 11 o'clock and at 3 o'clock, you can watch the bears eat lunch.
Please do not feed the animals.
Our animals have special food, and people food can make them sick.
Do not make a lot of noise near the animals.
Put your garbage in the bins.
Have a great day at the zoo!
Every Saturday, Mrs. Kim goes to the supermarket with her son, Jun.
Jun holds the shopping list, and his mother pushes the cart.
First, they buy fruit and vegetables: apples, bananas, potatoes and onions.
Then they get milk, cheese, yogurt and a big bottle of water.
Jun sees a box of chocolate cookies.
"Mom, can we buy these?" he asks.
His mother looks at the price.
"They are too expensive. Let's make cookies at home this afternoon."
Jun thinks it is a good idea.
So they buy sugar, butter and eggs.
At the end, Mrs. Kim pays with her credit card.
The cookies at home are delicious, and they are not expensive.
There is a music club at our school.
It meets every Tuesday after class in the music room.
Some students play the piano, and some play the guitar.
Two boys play the drums, and they make a lot of noise!
The other students sing.
Our teacher, Mr. Park, is a musician.
He plays in a band on the weekend.
He says music is like a language.
You can understand a song from any place in the world.
In December, the club has a big concert for the parents.
We practice for weeks.
On the night of the concert, we are a little afraid, but we sing our best.
Today, most homes have the internet.
People use it for many different things.
Children use it for homework.
They look for information about animals, history or science.
Parents read the news, pay for things and write emails.
Grandparents often use it to see photos of their family.
You can also watch videos, listen to music and play games online.
With a computer or a mobile phone, you can talk to a friend in another city.
But be careful.
Not all information on the internet is true.
Do not give your address or your password to people you do not know.
And turn off the screen and go outside sometimes!
The sea is very big.
Water covers most of our world, and most of this water is in the sea.
Sea water is salty, so we cannot drink it.
Many animals live in the sea.
There are small fish, big fish and very big animals like whales.
Some fish have beautiful colors: blue, yellow, orange and pink.
People use the sea, too.
Big ships carry things from one place to another.
Fishermen catch fish for our dinner.
In summer, families swim and play on the beach.
But today there is a lot of garbage in the sea.
Plastic bottles and bags can kill fish and birds.
We must keep the sea clean.
In England, December is a cold month.
The days are short, and it is dark at four o'clock in the afternoon.
People wear coats and hats, and sometimes there is snow.
But in Australia, December is in summer!
Australia is in the south of the world, so its seasons are different.
When it is winter in England, it is summer in Australia.
In Sydney, many people have Christmas lunch on the beach.
They eat cold food, like salad, fish and ice cream.
Children swim in the sea on Christmas Day.
In July, it is winter there, and people drink hot tea.
How do you travel to a new city?
You can go by plane, by train or by bus.
A plane is the fastest.
It is good for a long trip, but tickets are often expensive.
You also have to be at the airport early.
A train is slower, but it is comfortable.
You can walk around, eat and look out of the window.
Train stations are usually in the middle of the city.
A bus is the slowest, but it is the easiest on your money.
Some buses have free Wi-Fi.
On a long bus trip, bring a book, some water and a small pillow!
Firefighters have a very important job.
When there is a fire, they come fast in a big red truck.
They wear special clothes and a hat, because fire is very hot.
Firefighters do not only fight fires.
They help people after car accidents.
They help animals, too, like a cat at the top of a tree!
They also visit schools and teach children about fire.
At the fire station, firefighters sleep, cook and eat together.
They are like a big family.
When the bell rings, they stop everything and run to the truck.
Look at the map of our town.
In the middle, there is a big square with a clock tower.
The bank is on the left of the square.
The hotel is on the right.
Main Street goes from the square to the river.
On Main Street, there are shops, two cafes and a cinema.
The school is at the end of Main Street, near the bridge.
The train station is behind the hotel.
The hospital is on a hill, between the park and the church.
The supermarket is outside the town, so people go there by car or by bus.
It is a small town, but it has everything we need.
This park is for everyone.
Please help us keep it clean and beautiful.
Put your garbage in the bins.
There are bins for paper, glass and plastic.
Do not walk on the flowers.
Keep your dog on a lead, and clean up after it.
Do not feed the birds bread, because it is bad for them.
Bikes are OK on the path, but please ride slowly near children.
The park is open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.
On the first Saturday of every month, we clean the park together.
Come and join us!
A hundred years ago, children did not have computers or phones.
But they had toys, and they played every day.
Many toys were made of wood.
Children had small wooden trains, horses and boats.
Girls often had dolls with beautiful dresses.
A ball was a great toy for a group of friends.
On windy days, children flew kites in the fields.
Some children did not have money for toys.
So they made toys from old boxes, paper and stones.
They also played games like hide and seek.
Children still play some of these games today!
A sandwich is an easy and delicious lunch.
You need two pieces of bread, butter, cheese, a tomato and some chicken.
First, wash your hands.
Then put a little butter on the two pieces of bread.
Cut the tomato into thin circles with a knife.
Be careful, because the knife is sharp!
Put the cheese, the chicken and the tomato on one piece of bread.
Put the other piece on top.
Cut the sandwich in half.
Now your sandwich is ready.
You can eat it at home or take it to school in a box.
The Davis family has four people and five phones.
They look at their phones at breakfast, at lunch and at dinner.
One day, Mom has an idea.
"Let's try a day with no phones this Sunday," she says.
The children are not happy, but they say yes.
On Sunday morning, they put the phones in a box.
At first, it is strange and boring.
Then Dad finds some old board games.
They play together, and they laugh a lot.
In the afternoon, they ride their bikes to the river.
In the evening, they cook dinner together and talk for hours.
At night, the son says, "That was a good day."
Now the family has a day with no phones every month.
Lily's grandparents live in another city.
This week, they are coming to stay with Lily's family.
Lily is very excited.
She cleans her room and puts flowers on the table.
Grandma and Grandpa arrive on Monday evening by train.
They bring a lot of gifts: a book for Lily and a big cake for everyone.
Every morning, Grandpa and Lily walk in the park.
He tells her stories about her mother when she was a little girl.
In the afternoon, Grandma teaches Lily to cook soup.
On Sunday, they go back home.
Lily is sad, and she cries a little at the station.
"We will call you every week," Grandma says.
"And you can visit us in the summer!"
The Olympic Games are the biggest sports event in the world.
They happen every four years in a different city.
The first Olympics were in Greece a very long time ago.
Today, sports players from more than 200 places come to the Olympics.
They run, swim, jump, ride bikes and play many team sports.
The best players get gold, and other good players get prizes, too.
There are also Winter Olympics.
There, people ski and skate on snow and ice.
For many young players, going to the Olympics is a dream.
They practice every day for years.
For a long time, people wanted to fly like birds.
Two brothers, Orville and Wilbur Wright, had the same dream.
They had a bicycle shop in Ohio, in the United States.
The brothers read many books about birds and machines.
They built their own airplane in their shop.
Many times, it did not work, but they did not stop.
In December 1903, they took their plane to a windy beach in North Carolina.
Orville got in, and the plane went up into the air.
It flew for only twelve seconds.
But it was the first real airplane in history!
Do you have a job interview next week?
Here are some tips.
Before the interview, learn about the company.
Look at its website, and read some news about it.
Check your form and your letter for mistakes.
Make two copies, and put them in a file.
On the day, wear clean and simple clothes.
Arrive at the office ten minutes early.
When you meet the interviewer, smile and say, "It's a pleasure to meet you."
Answer every question in a clear and correct way.
Talk about your skills and your studies at college.
At the end, say, "Thank you. I'm glad to be here."
Good luck!
Welcome to the Sunny Park Swimming Pool.
The pool is open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. every day.
Please take a shower before you swim.
Wear a swimming cap if you have long hair.
Do not run near the pool, because the floor is wet.
Do not eat or drink in the water.
Children under eight must be with a parent.
The toilets and the bathrooms are behind the café.
Please keep them clean.
If you need help, call the lifeguard.
He or she is always near the pool.
Have fun, and be safe!
We give the Sea View Hotel 4 out of 5 stars.
We stayed at the Sea View Hotel for three nights in August.
The hotel is on a beautiful beach, and the rooms are large.
Our room had a lovely view of the sea.
The bed was very comfortable, and the bathroom was clean.
The breakfast was excellent.
There was fresh fruit, eggs, bread and very good coffee.
The pool was small, but the children loved it.
Maria at the front desk was very kind to our guests and to us.
There was one problem.
The hotel bar was noisy until one o'clock at night.
So bring something for your ears!
But we are going to stay here again next summer.
Our school has a newspaper called the Green Valley Times.
It comes out on the first Monday of every month.
Twelve students work on it, and our English teacher helps us.
The newspaper has four sections: school news, sports, art and fun.
Some students are reporters.
They interview teachers and students, and they write articles.
Other students take photos or draw pictures for the pages.
Every month, we have a survey.
Last month, students voted for the best school lunch.
The result? Pizza, of course!
Before we print the newspaper, we read every article two times.
We check the spelling and the grammar, and we correct every mistake.
On Saturday, our class visited an old palace outside the city.
A king and a queen lived there four hundred years ago.
The palace is very large, and it has two hundred rooms.
A guide showed us the rooms.
In the big hall, there were paintings of the king and his family.
The little prince and princess had beautiful clothes.
But they did not smile.
"People did not smile in paintings then," said the guide.
In the garden, there was a small temple and a lake with white birds.
The guide told us about a war long ago.
After the war, the king made peace with his enemy in this garden.
It was a great day, and now history is my favorite subject!
Do you like drama?
Come and join our theater club!
We meet every Wednesday at four o'clock in the school hall.
Every year, we put on a play.
This year, the play is about a lonely ghost in an old house.
There are roles for twelve actors.
Some characters are funny, and some are strange.
You do not have to be an actor.
We also need singers, dancers and people to paint the stage.
Our teacher, Mrs. Bell, says drama is good for shy students.
You learn to speak in front of people.
The play is on the last Friday in March.
Bring your family and friends!
Good health starts with good habits.
A habit is something you do every day.
Brush your teeth two times a day, in the morning and before bed.
Wash your hands before you eat and after you use the toilet.
Dirty hands can make you sick.
Eat fruit and vegetables every day, and do not eat too much candy.
Do some exercise for thirty minutes a day.
You can walk, dance, swim or ride a bike.
Some habits are bad for your health.
Smoking is very bad for your heart.
Sitting on the couch all day is not healthy, too.
If you have a fever or a bad headache, see a doctor.
Do not take medicine without a doctor's help.
Look carefully at a garden, and you can see a lot of small animals.
In the sunshine, bees fly from flower to flower.
They are very busy, and they make honey.
Butterflies visit the flowers, too.
They have beautiful colors on their wings.
Near the water, there are frogs.
A frog can jump very far with its long back legs.
Birds eat small animals in the grass, and a mouse lives under the old wood.
At night, bats fly over the yard.
They eat a lot of small flying animals.
If you dig in the garden, you can find other small animals in the ground.
Please be kind to them, because every animal helps the garden.
Hi Tom!
Here is the way to the new bookstore from the subway station.
When you come out of the station, turn left.
Walk straight for two blocks.
You can see a big supermarket on the corner.
Turn right there, into Oak Street.
The bookstore is beside the post office.
Its name is Page Turner, and there is a big red book above the door.
There is a café inside, below the store, too.
It takes about ten minutes to walk.
See you there at three!
Lily
People speak English in America and in Britain.
But some words are different.
In America, a child calls his mother "Mom."
In Britain, he says "Mum."
Americans wear pants, but British people wear trousers.
In Britain, "pants" are the clothes under your trousers!
With a cup of tea, an American eats a cookie, and a British person eats a biscuit.
In New York, you take the subway, but in London, you take the tube.
Americans live in an apartment, and British people live in a flat.
The biggest difference is sports.
In Britain, football is played with the feet.
In America, that game is soccer, and football is a different sport!
What do you want to be in the future?
Many jobs today are very old: doctor, teacher, farmer and driver.
But technology is changing the world of work.
Today, many people write code.
They make programs for computers and phones.
Engineers design robots for factories and hospitals.
Scientists study the sea, the sky and the human body.
In the future, there are going to be new jobs.
Maybe you are going to be a space driver or a farmer on a tall building!
Some skills are always important: speaking well, working in a team and solving problems.
So, keep learning and keep asking questions!
Good afternoon, everyone!
Let me introduce myself.
My first name is Pedro, and my last name is Silva.
I am a foreign student from Brazil, so my nationality is Brazilian.
My hometown is São Paulo.
It is a very large city with a lot of tall buildings.
I am sixteen, and I am in Class 11C.
My hobby is surfing.
I also like tennis and fishing.
My English is OK, but sometimes I do not understand fast conversation.
So if I say "Pardon?" please say it again slowly.
I am glad to be your classmate.
Thank you, and bye for now!
Dear Mom and Dad,
I am having a great time at summer camp!
We arrived yesterday afternoon after four hours on the bus.
The camp is on a farm near a river, and there are sheep and horses everywhere.
I am in a room with my cousin Jake and two other boys.
Every day, there are a lot of activities.
This morning, we rode horses, and in the afternoon, we went fishing.
I caught a fish, but it was very small, so I put it back in the water.
Tonight, we are going to sing songs and tell ghost stories.
I am lucky, because the weather is sunny.
I enjoy camp, but I miss you and our dog, Cooper.
I hope you are all well.
I wish you were here!
Love, Emma
This year, we have a new English teacher, Ms. Gray.
At first, everyone thought she was very strict.
In her class, you cannot be late, and you cannot be rude.
If you are lazy, she says, "You can do better than that."
But now I like her very much.
She makes lessons interesting.
Every week, we discuss a new topic, like food, sports or the future.
She gives us an example, and then we write our own sentences.
We use a dictionary for new words, and we underline them in our notebooks.
When we make a mistake, she asks us to repeat the word slowly.
Ms. Gray listens to our ideas, too.
Last month, I had a suggestion for a class trip, and she agreed!
My grades are better now.
Maybe a strict teacher is not a bad thing.
Carlos has a lot of hair.
It is long, and it goes into his eyes.
"You need a haircut," his mother says every day.
On Saturday, Carlos goes to Tony's shop on the corner.
Tony is a funny man with no hair on his head.
"Guess why I am a hair cutter," he says, and he laughs.
Carlos sits in the big chair.
Tony works fast, and hair falls on the floor.
After twenty minutes, Carlos looks in the mirror.
His hair is very short now.
"I look strange," he says.
"No, you look handsome," says Tony.
At home, his little sister says, "You look cute!"
Carlos is not sure about "cute," but he likes his new haircut.
Now he can see everything!
It is Mr. and Mrs. Martin's wedding day, but twenty years later.
To celebrate, they go to a nice restaurant with their daughter.
The dining room is quiet, and there are flowers on every table.
A waiter brings them the menu.
Mrs. Martin orders fish with rice, and Mr. Martin orders a steak.
Their daughter wants a hamburger.
"This is a nice restaurant," says her mother. "Are you sure?"
"Yes," says the girl. "A burger is my favorite food."
The waiter smiles. "Our burgers are very good," he says.
The food is delicious.
After dinner, a waitress named Rosa brings a small cake with a candle.
"Happy anniversary!" she says.
Mrs. Martin looks at her husband.
"Did you tell them?" she asks.
"No," he says. "I think our daughter did."
The girl smiles and eats her burger.
My grandfather has a big old album.
In it, there are more than a thousand stamps.
He started his collection when he was fourteen years old.
In the past, people sent a lot of mail.
There was no email, and a telephone call to another country was expensive.
So people wrote letters, and every letter had a stamp.
Grandpa's friends and family sent him stamps from everywhere.
Some stamps have pictures of kings and queens.
Some have birds, flowers, ships or famous buildings.
My favorite is a small blue stamp with a jet on it.
Every stamp is a memory for Grandpa.
When he shows me the album, he tells me a story about each one.
In some big cities, the air is dirty.
On bad days, the sky is gray, but it is not cloudy.
It is air pollution.
Where does it come from?
Cars and trucks make a lot of smoke.
Some factories make smoke, too.
When there is no wind, the smoke stays over the city.
When the wind blows, the air gets clean again.
Dirty air is bad for our health.
It can hurt our eyes, and it can make it hard to breathe.
What can we do?
We can walk, ride a bike or take the bus.
We can plant trees, because trees help to clean the air.
My mother is a nurse at the city hospital.
She works in the children's section.
Some weeks she works in the day, and some weeks she works at night.
It is a difficult job.
A nurse has many jobs.
My mother checks the children's temperature, and she gives them medicine.
She talks to worried parents, and she helps the doctors.
She uses a lot of tools and machines.
She is on her feet all day.
My father is a police officer, so he understands her job.
When she comes home tired, he makes dinner.
I am her daughter, and I am very proud of her.
One day, I want to help people like she does.
Sofia needs a new skirt for her school concert.
It has to be black.
On Saturday, she goes to a clothes store with her aunt.
There is a big sale, and many things are half price.
Sofia finds a nice black skirt.
She takes it to the room at the back and puts it on.
It is too tight!
"What size is it?" asks her aunt.
"Small," says Sofia.
Her aunt finds the same skirt in a medium size.
This one is perfect.
Her aunt also buys her a pair of black shoes.
"The shoes are my gift for your concert," she says.
Sofia is very happy.
"Thank you! Can you come to the concert, too?" she asks.
"Of course," says her aunt.
Numbers are everywhere in our lives.
When you wake up, you look at the clock.
It is a quarter past seven, or 7:15.
In the kitchen, a recipe says, "Add two cups of milk."
At the shop, a T-shirt costs fourteen dollars.
Numbers help us in math class, too.
Here is an easy sum: 20 + 70 = 90.
Twenty and seventy is ninety.
Half of ninety is forty-five.
Some numbers are special.
There are seven days in a week and twelve months in a year.
September is the ninth month.
A football team has eleven players.
What is your lucky number?
Do you want to write a poem?
It is not difficult.
You can be a writer, too!
First, choose a topic.
It can be about anything: the sea, your cat or a happy memory.
Then close your eyes and imagine it.
What can you see?
What can you hear and smell?
How is your feeling?
Now write some short lines.
Describe the colors, the sounds and your feelings.
You do not need long sentences.
Here is an example: "The sea is blue. / The wind is cool. / I am happy here."
Read your poem out loud.
Change some words if you want to.
Then share it with a friend!
Good students ask a lot of questions.
Questions help us learn and understand.
In English, many questions start with a special word.
"Who" is for people: "Who is your teacher?"
"Whose" is for things that are someone's: "Whose bag is this?"
"Which" is for a choice: "Which color do you want, red or blue?"
"When" is for time, and "where" is for places.
"Why" asks for a reason: "Why are you late?"
"How" asks about the way: "How do you go to school?"
Could you ask a question about this text?
Try it now!
The day of your birth is special everywhere.
But every culture has its own birthday celebration.
In Mexico, there is often a colorful paper animal full of candy.
Children hit it with a stick until the candy falls out.
In Korea, people eat seaweed soup on their birthday.
In China, long noodles are a birthday food, because they mean a long life.
In Canada, some people put butter on a child's nose for good luck!
In Denmark, families put a flag in the window.
Many people also have a cake with candles.
The number of candles is your age.
You make a wish, and you blow out the candles.
How do you celebrate your birthday?
We spend about a third of our lives asleep.
That seems like a lot of time, but sleep is not wasted time.
While we sleep, our body is very busy.
First, sleep helps the body to grow and repair itself.
Children and teenagers grow mostly at night.
Sleep is also important for the brain.
During the day, we learn a lot of new things.
At night, the brain sorts this information and stores the most important parts.
That is why a good night's sleep before an exam is better than studying until midnight.
When people do not sleep enough, they feel tired and in a bad mood.
They make more mistakes, and they get ill more easily.
So if you have a lot of work tomorrow, the best thing you can do tonight is go to bed.
Look at your breakfast table this morning.
Your food probably traveled a long way to get there.
The orange juice may come from oranges grown in Spain or Brazil.
The coffee beans may come from a farm in Vietnam or Kenya.
Some fruit travels by plane, so it arrives fresh.
Other food travels by ship for several weeks.
Of course, a lot of our food is local.
Milk, eggs and bread often come from farms and factories near our town.
Local food is usually cheaper, and it does not need so much transport.
Next time you go shopping, look at the labels.
You can learn a lot about the world from your shopping basket!
Learning a new language is not easy, but it is one of the most useful things you can do.
Here are some ideas that really work.
Study a little every day.
Fifteen minutes every day is better than two hours once a week.
Learn new vocabulary in groups, like food words or travel words.
Then use the new words in your own sentences.
Listen as much as you can.
Watch videos, listen to songs and try to repeat what you hear.
This helps you improve your pronunciation.
Do not be afraid of mistakes.
Everyone makes mistakes when they speak a new language.
If you can, find a language partner and talk every week.
Finally, be patient.
After a few months, you will feel more confident, and you will be surprised at how much you understand.
Do you often have no money at the end of the month?
You are not alone.
Here are some simple ways to save money.
First, write down everything you spend for two weeks.
Many people are surprised when they see their list.
Small things, like a coffee every morning, cost a lot in a year.
Then make a budget.
Decide how much you can spend on food, transport and fun.
When you get your money, put some of it in a savings account first.
Even a little money every month grows over time.
Before you buy something expensive, compare prices online and wait a few days.
Ask yourself, "Do I really need this?"
Often, the answer is no.
Laura Díaz is a pilot for a large airline.
Her working day often starts very early.
Today, she wakes up at four o'clock in the morning.
She arrives at the airport two hours before her flight to Paris.
First, she meets the other pilot and the cabin crew.
They check the weather, the plane and the plan for the flight.
The flight takes two hours.
Most of the time, the plane flies on automatic, but the pilots must watch everything carefully.
Landing is the most difficult part, especially in bad weather.
After Paris, Laura flies to London and then back home to Madrid.
She gets home at eight o'clock in the evening.
"It's a tiring job," she says, "but I love the view from my office!"
The Great Wall of China is one of the most famous buildings in the world.
It is not one wall, but many walls.
People built them over about two thousand years.
Long ago, the land in the north of China was often attacked.
So the Chinese kings built walls to protect their kingdom.
Soldiers lived in towers on the wall, and they watched for enemies.
When they saw danger, they lit fires to send a message to the next tower.
The walls cross mountains, deserts and rivers.
All together, they are thousands of kilometers long.
Today, millions of tourists visit the wall every year.
Some parts are in very good condition, but other parts are now ruins.
Packing can be stressful, especially when you are in a hurry.
Here is some advice to make it easier.
Start with a list.
Check the weather in the place you are visiting, and choose clothes for it.
Choose clothes that go well together, so you can wear them in different ways.
Roll your clothes instead of folding them.
They take less space, and they do not get creased.
Put heavy things, like shoes, at the bottom of your suitcase.
Keep important things in your hand luggage: your passport, your money, your phone and its charger.
Take a copy of your passport, too, in case you lose it.
Finally, leave some empty space.
You will probably want to bring something home!
What will cities look like in fifty years?
Nobody knows exactly, but engineers and designers have many ideas.
In the city of the future, there may be fewer cars on the roads.
People will travel by electric bus, by tram or by bike.
Some cars will drive themselves.
There will be more parks and trees, because they keep the air clean and cool.
Buildings may have gardens on their roofs and walls.
People may even grow vegetables on the fortieth floor!
Homes will use energy from the sun and the wind.
Of course, the future also brings problems.
More people will live in cities, so there will be less space.
Good cities will need good planning.
An earthquake happens when the ground starts to shake.
But why does the ground move?
The earth's surface is made of very big pieces of rock called plates.
These plates move very slowly, only a few centimeters every year.
Two plates can get stuck.
Pressure builds up for many years, and then the rock suddenly breaks.
The ground shakes, and the shaking travels through the earth.
Most earthquakes are small, and people do not even feel them.
But a strong earthquake can destroy buildings and roads.
In countries like Japan, buildings are designed to move a little without breaking.
Children practice what to do at school.
If you feel an earthquake, get under a strong table and hold on.

Millions of people use social media every day.
They share photos, watch videos and chat with friends.
But is social media good for us?
There are some clear advantages.
Social media helps us to stay in contact with friends and family who live far away.
It is also a quick way to get news and to learn new things.
Small businesses can use it to find customers.
However, there are disadvantages, too.
Some people spend hours looking at their phones instead of talking to the people around them.
Not all the information online is true.
And when people only see perfect photos of other people's lives, they can feel unhappy about their own.
In my opinion, social media is a useful tool.
The important thing is to use it, not to let it use you.
A honeybee lives in a hive with up to sixty thousand other bees.
Every bee has a job.
The queen is the biggest bee in the hive.
Her only job is to lay eggs, and she can lay two thousand eggs in one day.
Most of the bees are workers.
Young workers clean the hive and feed the babies.
Older workers fly out to find flowers.
When a bee finds a lot of flowers, it goes back to the hive and does a special dance.
The dance tells the other bees the direction and the distance to the flowers.
Bees are very important for people, too.
As they move from flower to flower, they help plants to produce fruit and seeds.
Without bees, we would have much less food.
My grandmother, Hoa, was born in a small village in 1950.
Last weekend, I asked her about her childhood, and she told me a lot of stories.
When she was a girl, there was no electricity in her village.
At night, the family used oil lamps.
There was no television, so the children played outside until dark.
They made their own toys from wood and paper.
Her school was four kilometers from her house, and she walked there every day.
In the rainy season, the path was full of mud, and the journey took even longer.
After school, she helped her parents in the rice fields.
Life was hard, but my grandmother says she was happy.
"We didn't have much," she said, "but we had time for each other."
I thought about that for a long time.
Every year, each person throws away hundreds of kilos of rubbish.
A lot of it could have a second life.
That is why recycling is so important.
It is easy to recycle at home.
Put paper, plastic, glass and metal in separate bins.
Wash bottles and cans before you recycle them.
Food waste can go into a compost bin in the garden.
After a few months, it becomes rich soil for your plants.
Recycling is good, but it is even better to use less.
Take your own bag when you go shopping.
Carry a water bottle instead of buying plastic bottles.
Repair old things instead of throwing them away.
Small changes in every home can make a big difference.
Today, most people carry a phone in their pocket.
But the first telephone was invented less than 150 years ago.
Alexander Graham Bell was born in Scotland in 1847.
His mother could not hear well, and his father taught people how to speak clearly.
So Bell was interested in sound and the human voice from a young age.
Later, he moved to America and became a teacher of deaf students.
In his free time, Bell tried to send the human voice through an electric wire.
In March 1876, he finally succeeded.
He spoke into his machine, "Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you."
His assistant, Thomas Watson, heard the words clearly in another room.
It was the first telephone call in history.
Many people think that healthy food is expensive.
But you can eat well without spending a lot of money.
Plan your meals for the week before you go shopping.
Then buy only what is on your list.
Buy fruit and vegetables that are in season.
They are cheaper and they taste better.
Frozen vegetables are a good choice, too: they are healthy, and they last a long time.
Beans, lentils, rice and eggs are cheap, and they give you a lot of energy.
Cook at home as often as you can.
Fast food and ready meals cost much more than simple home cooking.
Compare the prices in different shops, because the same food can cost much less at the market.
Instead of buying snacks, take some fruit with you.
If you cook a big pot of soup, you can eat it for two or three days.
And do not go to the supermarket when you are hungry!
You will always buy more than you need, and your bill will be bigger!
Museum Night at the City Art Museum

Today, many people work from home for some or all of the week.
Is it better than working in an office?
Working from home has some big advantages.
You do not waste time and money on the journey to work, and you do not sit in traffic.
You can start work earlier or later, and you can wear what you want.
Many people say they can concentrate better at home, because the office is noisy.
But there are disadvantages, too.
Some people feel lonely without their colleagues.
Online meetings are useful, but they are not the same as talking face to face.
It can be hard to stop working at the end of the day, because your office is in your home.
And when there are children or pets in the house, it is not always quiet!
For many workers, the best answer is a mix: a few days at home and a few days in the office.
What do you think of when you hear the word "desert"?
Most people imagine sand, sun and very hot days.
The Sahara in Africa is like that.
It is the largest hot desert in the world, and in summer it can be over 50 degrees.
But a desert is not always hot.
A desert is a place that gets very little rain or snow.
So Antarctica, the coldest place on earth, is also a desert!
In many hot deserts, the nights are very cold, because there are no clouds to keep the heat in.
Life in the desert is difficult, but many plants and animals live there.
Some plants keep water in their thick leaves.
Many animals sleep in the day and come out at night, when it is cooler.
Do you ever touch wood for good luck?
Many people do, even when they say they do not believe in superstitions.
In many countries, the number thirteen is unlucky.
Some tall buildings do not have a thirteenth floor.
In Italy, seventeen is the unlucky number, and in China, it is four.
In China, the word for "four" sounds like the word for "death."
Some superstitions are about animals.
In Britain, some people think a black cat brings bad luck, but others think it brings good luck!
In Russia, people sit down quietly for a moment before a long journey.
They believe it brings a safe trip.
Are these ideas true?
Probably not, but they are an interesting part of every culture.

More and more people shop online.
You can buy almost anything on the internet, from books to furniture.
But is it better than going to a real shop?
Online shopping is convenient.
You can do it at any time, and you do not have to leave your house.
It is easy to compare prices, so you can often find cheaper products.
You can also read reviews from other customers before you buy.
On the other hand, you cannot touch or try things before you buy them.
Clothes may be the wrong size, and colors often look different in real life.
Sometimes delivery takes a long time.
And when everyone shops online, small local shops may close.
So many people now use both: online for some things and local shops for others.
Many animals around the world are endangered.
This means there are so few of them that they may disappear forever.
Why is this happening?
The biggest reason is that animals are losing their homes.
People cut down forests to build farms, roads and cities.
Some animals are hunted for their skin, their meat or their horns.
Pollution and climate change are also serious problems.
Tigers in Asia and elephants in Africa are two famous examples.
But there is some good news.
In some national parks, the number of tigers is slowly increasing.
Scientists, governments and local people are working together to protect them.
You can help, too, by learning about these animals and telling others.
Last September, my family moved to a new city, and I had to change schools.
I was very nervous on my first day.
I didn't know anyone, and the school was much bigger than my old one.
I was worried that nobody would talk to me.
In the morning, I got lost and arrived late for my first lesson.
Everyone looked at me when I opened the door.
My face went red.
But the teacher smiled and said, "Welcome! Sit next to Mateo. He'll help you."
Mateo was very kind.
At lunchtime, he showed me the cafeteria and introduced me to his friends.
We talked about football and computer games, and I started to relax.
After school, I told my mum, "It wasn't as bad as I expected."
Now, a year later, Mateo is my best friend, and I feel confident at my new school.
Police are looking for two men after a robbery at a jewelry shop downtown on Tuesday night.
The thieves broke the glass door at about eleven o'clock and stole diamond rings and gold watches.
The shop's alarm rang, but by the time the police arrived, the men were gone.
A security guard in the building next door saw a black car drive away at high speed.
"I heard a loud noise, and then silence," he said.
"It was a shock. This is usually a very quiet area."
The owner, Mrs. Mills, said the missing jewelry is worth about fifty thousand dollars.
Police officers are checking cameras on Oak Street for evidence.
An official said, "This kind of crime is rare here."
"But we ask all citizens to lock their doors and report anything unusual," the official added.
If you have any information, please contact the police station.
Rating: four stars
The Last Lighthouse is the latest film from the director Ana Ruiz, and it was released in cinemas last Friday.
The story is about an old man who lives alone in a lighthouse on a wild coast.
One stormy night, a young woman appears at his door, and she has a secret.
I won't tell you the ending!
The film is not a horror movie, but some scenes are quite frightening.
There is also a little romance and a few jokes.
