Tom Blake gives a brilliant performance as the old man, and the landscape is fantastic.
The only problem is the middle of the film, which is a bit slow.
But the audience in my cinema was completely silent at the end.
Go and see it!
Last Saturday, the Riverside Rockets won the national basketball championship for the first time.
More than twenty thousand fans were in the stadium for the final against Lakeside.
The game was very close.
At half time, the Rockets were behind by eight points, and many fans were worried.
But in the second half, the team's captain, Jess Owusu, played the best basketball of her life.
She scored thirty points, which is a new record for a final.
With ten seconds left, she hit the winning shot, and the crowd went crazy.
After the game, the players received their gold medals and the award for the season's best team.
"We trained every day for this," said Owusu.
"This success belongs to the whole team and to our fans."
Many people dream of starting their own business.
It can be exciting, but it is also a big challenge.
Here is some basic advice.
First, choose a product or a service that people really need.
Look at the local market.
Who are your customers, and what do other businesses already offer?
Think of a good name for your brand.
Next, make a budget.
How much money do you need at the beginning, and how long will it take to earn it back?
Keep every bill and every receipt, and record the cash that comes in and goes out.
You do not need a lot of money for advertising.
A simple website and social media can bring your first customers.
Finally, remember that most businesses do not succeed in the first year.
Learn from your mistakes, and do not give up too early.
Almost two million people live in our capital city, and the population is growing every year.
I live in an apartment downtown, right in the center.
There are many advantages.
Everything is near: shops, restaurants, the main square and the bus station.
I don't need a car, so I don't have to find a space in a car park.
The public transport is good, and the trams run every five minutes.
There is a big department store at the end of my street, with an escalator and glass elevators.
But the center is crowded and noisy.
The traffic is heavy all day, especially on the highway into the city.
Rent is very expensive, and my apartment is small.
Some areas are now car-free zones, and I think that is a great idea.
Maybe one day the whole center will be quiet.
Everyone has good days and bad days.
Our feelings change all the time, and that is normal.
Sometimes we feel anxious before an exam or an important event.
We may feel upset when a friend says something unkind.
When we are tired or hungry, small things can be very annoying.
Feelings like envy or fear are not bad; they are messages.
They tell us that something is important to us.
Psychologists say it helps to give a name to your feeling.
Instead of "I feel bad," try saying "I feel embarrassed" or "I feel disappointed."
Then think about why you feel like that.
Talking to someone you trust is also very helpful.
And remember the good feelings, too: joy, pride and happiness.
Be grateful for them!
My husband and I went on a cruise around the Greek islands in June.
It was our first time abroad in ten years, and it was unforgettable.
The ship, the Blue Star, had more than two thousand passengers.
Our cabin was small but comfortable, and it had a balcony with a view of the sea.
Every morning, we arrived at a new island.
We went sightseeing with our guidebook, walked along the shore and swam in quiet bays.
The scenery was amazing: white villages, blue water and sandy beaches.
There were a few negative things.
The food on the ship was expensive, and the ship was very crowded at dinner time.
But for travelers who want to see a lot of places in one journey, a cruise is a good choice.
This soup is healthy, cheap and easy to make.
It is perfect for a cold winter evening.
You need: one onion, two cloves of garlic, three carrots, a cup of peas, some mushrooms, olive oil, salt and pepper.
First, slice the onion and the carrots, and cut the garlic into very small pieces.
Put a large pan on the stove and pour in two spoons of olive oil.
Fry the onion and the garlic for three minutes.
Then add the carrots, the mushrooms and one liter of water.
Wait until the water boils.
Cook the soup for twenty minutes, then add the peas.
After five more minutes, add salt and pepper.
Serve the soup hot with fresh bread.
If you have some left, you can keep it in the fridge for two days.
Last month, my sister Laura and I moved into a new apartment on the fifth floor.
The rent is higher than in our old place, but it is much bigger.
When you enter, there is a long hall with a cupboard for coats and shoes.
The sitting room has two armchairs, a sofa and a tall bookcase.
Its big windows open onto a balcony, where we have breakfast when it is sunny.
The kitchen is modern, with a new cooker, a large fridge and a washing machine.
The sink is under the window, so I can look at the trees while I do the washing-up.
There are two bedrooms.
Mine is quite small, but it has a desk with drawers, so I can work there.
The heating is good, which is important in winter.
The only problem is the elevator.
It is often broken, so we have to walk up the stairs!
For three days, Ben had a terrible toothache.
He could not eat, and he could not sleep.
Finally, his mother made an appointment with the dentist.
Ben was very nervous in the waiting room.
He hated the sound of the dentist's drill.
The receptionist smiled at him and said, "Don't worry. Dr. Patel is very gentle."
Dr. Patel looked inside Ben's mouth with a small mirror.
"You have a hole in this tooth," she said. "Do you eat a lot of sweets?"
Ben's cheeks went red.
She told him to relax and to breathe slowly.
The treatment took twenty minutes, and it hurt a bit, but not much.
When it was finished, Dr. Patel gave Ben a new toothbrush.
"Brush twice a day, and eat fewer sweets," she said.
"You were very brave."
A powerful storm hit the north of the country on Sunday night.
It rained heavily for more than ten hours, and there were strong winds and a thunderstorm.
The wind destroyed several roofs and broke branches from many trees.
In the park, an old oak tree fell across the path.
Some roads were flooded, and a few villages had no power until Monday afternoon.
Emergency workers were busy all night.
They helped elderly people to leave their homes and took them to a safe building.
Luckily, nobody died, but two people were injured by falling glass.
On Monday morning, the weather was calm again, and the sun came out.
People came out of their houses to see the damage and to help their neighbors.
Experts say that storms like this will become more common in the future.
When you learn English, you often need words to talk about the language itself.
Here are some of the most useful ones.
A noun is a word for a person, a place or a thing, like "teacher," "city" or "book."
A verb is an action word, like "run" or "think."
An adjective describes a noun: "a red car," "a happy child."
Most nouns have a singular form and a plural form, such as "cat" and "cats."
Adjectives have comparative and superlative forms: "big, bigger, the biggest."
Every sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with punctuation, like a full stop or a question mark.
Pronunciation is how we say a word.
English spelling does not always show you how to pronounce a word correctly.
So it is a good idea to listen to new vocabulary, not only to read it.
In many countries, a new law begins as an idea.
Perhaps citizens are worried about an issue, like dangerous traffic near schools.
They write to politicians, or they sign a public request.
Then a group of politicians, called a committee, studies the problem.
The chairman of the committee asks experts for their opinion.
The committee writes a first version of the law and explains its purpose.
Next, there is a debate in parliament.
Some politicians support the new law, and others are against it.
Each side gives its arguments, and sometimes the discussion continues for weeks.
The law may change many times.
Finally, the politicians vote.
If most of them accept it, the law is passed.
The government makes an official statement, and the new law becomes part of the country's legal system.
It is a slow process, but it gives everyone a chance to be heard.
Your teacher has asked you to write an essay about a topic you know nothing about.
Where do you start?
First, find good sources of information.
Books from the library are usually reliable, because an author and an editor have checked them.
On the internet, be careful.
Look for well-known websites, like universities or national newspapers.
Anybody can write anything online, so check every fact in two or three places.
Take notes while you read.
Write down the title, the author and the page number, so you can find the information again later.
Do not copy whole paragraphs.
Use your own words instead.
When you have enough knowledge about the topic, make a plan.
Divide your essay into an introduction, three or four main parts and a summary.
The quality of your research will show in your writing.
The first Olympic Games took place in Olympia, in ancient Greece, almost three thousand years ago.
They were held every four years to honor Zeus, the king of the gods.
At first, there was only one event: a running race of about two hundred meters.
Later, there were many more, like wrestling, jumping and races with horses.
Only free men from Greek cities could take part.
Women were not allowed to compete, and married women could not even watch.
The winners did not receive gold or silver medals.
Instead, they got a crown made of olive leaves.
But when they went home, they were treated like heroes, and their cities gave them money and food for life.
During the games, wars between cities stopped, so people could travel safely.
The modern Olympic Games started again in 1896, and they continue this ancient tradition of peace.
Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist.
It beats about a hundred thousand times every day to push blood around your body.
Heart disease is one of the most common causes of death in the world, but there is a lot you can do to prevent it.
Physical activity is very important.
Doctors say adults should do at least thirty minutes of exercise, five days a week.
It does not have to be difficult: fast walking or cycling is enough.
A healthy diet helps, too.
Eat plenty of fruit, vegetables and fish, and use less salt, sugar and fat.
Keep your weight at a normal level, and do not smoke.
Stress can also have a bad effect on your heart, so find time to relax.
Finally, have a medical check regularly.
A doctor can measure your blood pressure and your heart rate.
Small changes in your daily life can make a big difference.
Fashion changes very quickly nowadays.
Every few weeks, shops sell new styles, and prices are often very low.
You can buy a T-shirt for the same price as a sandwich.
But how is this possible?
Most cheap clothes are made in large factories in poorer countries.
The workers there often earn very little money, and they work long hours.
The material is often cheap, too, so the clothes do not last long.
After a few washes, they lose their shape and color.
This has an impact on the environment.
Making clothes uses a lot of water and energy, and millions of tons of clothes are thrown away every year.
Some brands are trying to improve.
They use recycled material and pay their workers more.
As customers, we can help by buying fewer clothes of better quality.
Maya Ellis is the author of eight novels and many short stories.
We asked her about her work.
When did you start writing?
When I was a child, I kept a diary, and I invented adventures for my toys.
My first novel was published when I was thirty-five, after many rejections.
Where do your ideas come from?
Everywhere. A conversation on a bus, an old photograph, a strange dream.
I always carry a small notebook, because inspiration can come at any moment.
What is a normal working day for you?
I write from seven until noon, and I try to write a thousand words a day.
Some days, the words come easily. Other days, every sentence is a fight.
What advice do you have for young writers?
Read a lot, and do not be afraid of bad first drafts.
Every good book was a bad book first.
Our solar system has eight planets that travel around the sun.
The four planets closest to the sun are small and made of rock: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
Mercury is the smallest planet, and it has no air.
Venus is the hottest, because its thick clouds keep the heat in.
The temperature on Venus is more than four hundred degrees.
Mars is called the red planet because of the red dust on its surface.
Scientists believe that water existed on Mars long ago.
The four outer planets are enormous, and they are made mostly of gas.
Jupiter is so big that more than a thousand Earths could fit inside it.
Saturn is famous for its beautiful rings of ice and rock.
Uranus and Neptune are so far away that they are extremely cold.
There is still so much we do not know, and spaceships continue to explore them today.
Choosing an occupation is one of the biggest decisions in your life.
How do you know which job is right for you?
Start by thinking about your interests and your abilities.
Do you enjoy working with people, with numbers or with your hands?
Do you prefer to work in a team or alone?
Some people have a talent for art; others are good at solving problems.
Then find out as much as you can about different jobs.
Talk to professionals, like a nurse, an engineer or a hotel manager, and ask about a typical day.
If you can, get some experience.
A part-time job or a week in a company can show you what the work is really like.
Remember that money is important, but it is not everything.
You will spend many hours at work, so choose something that gives you a sense of purpose.
And do not worry if you change your mind later.
Many people change careers several times.
Why do people keep their money in a bank instead of under the bed?
First of all, it is safer.
If there is a fire or a robbery at your house, your money in the bank is not lost.
When you open an account, you get a bank card.
With it, you can take out cash, pay in shops and pay bills online.
Many people now use their phones instead of coins and notes.
Banks also pay you interest.
This means that if you keep your money in a savings account, the bank adds a little extra money every year.
How can they do that?
The bank lends your money to other people and businesses, and they pay the bank back with interest.
A credit card is different.
You spend the bank's money, and you pay it back later.
If you pay late, you have to pay a fee and a lot of interest.
So use it carefully!
Why are some places on our planet hot, while others are cold?
The main reason is the sun.
Near the middle of the globe, the sun's rays are strong all year, so it is warm.
In the far north and the far south, the rays are weak, and it is very cold.
The sea also changes the weather.
Places on the coast have milder temperatures than places in the middle of a continent.
In summer, the sea keeps the land cool, and in winter it keeps it warm.
Islands in the Pacific Ocean, for example, are warm but rarely extremely hot.
Mountains are another factor.
The higher you go, the colder it gets.
That is why there is snow on some mountains in hot countries.
Scientists say our world is slowly getting warmer.
The average temperature has risen by more than one degree in the last hundred years.
You do not need an expensive camera to take good photographs.
Most photographers agree that the most important things are light and practice.
Light changes everything in photography.
The best time to take photos outside is early in the morning or just before sunset.
At midday, the sun is too strong, and it makes hard shadows on people's faces.
If you take a portrait, put your friend in the shade, or near a window.
Think about the background, too.
A simple background makes the person or the object in your image stand out.
Do not always put your subject in the middle of the frame.
Try moving it a little to the left or right.
Finally, take a lot of pictures.
Look at them on a big screen at home and ask yourself what works and what does not.
Every photographer learns by making mistakes.
Friendship is one of the most important things in life.
But what makes a good friend?
For me, the most important thing is trust.
A good friend keeps your secrets and tells you the truth, even when it is difficult.
A good friend also supports you when you have problems.
They listen, and they do not always try to give advice.
Of course, friends sometimes argue.
That is normal, because people have different personalities and different opinions.
What matters is how you behave after an argument.
A good friend is able to say, "I'm sorry," and to forgive.
Finally, a good friend has a positive attitude.
They are happy about your success, and they are not jealous.
I am lucky to have a few friends like this.
I hope I am that kind of friend, too.
Last Sunday, my friend Nadia and I took the early train to the seaside.
When we arrived, there was a thick fog over the water, and it was quite cold.
But by eleven o'clock, the fog had gone.
There was bright daylight and a warm breeze.
We put on our swimsuits and sunglasses and ran into the sea.
The water was colder than we expected, and Nadia screamed when a wave splashed her face!
After that, we lay on the sand and floated in the calm water near the shore.
Some people were sailing small boats, and a few brave ones were surfing.
At lunchtime, we bought fish and chips from a small café near the beach.
An old fisherman sat on a bench next to us and told us stories about the sea.
In the afternoon, we collected shells and had ice cream and cold lemonade.
We were sleepy and a little burned by the sun on the train home.
But it was the best day of the summer.
When the snow comes, many people head to the mountains.
Winter sports are exciting, but they can also be dangerous if you are a beginner.
Skiing is the most popular winter sport.
Skiers go down the mountain on two long, thin skis.
Snowboarding is similar, but you stand on one wide board, like a surfer.
Many young people prefer it because it feels more free.
Ice skating is another favorite.
In some cities, there are outdoor rinks in the main square every winter.
Ice hockey is a fast team sport on skates, and it is very popular in Canada.
Before you try any winter sport, take a lesson with a teacher.
Wear a helmet, warm gloves and a scarf, and put sun cream on your face.
The sun is very strong in the mountains, even when it is freezing.
Yesterday I had to send a birthday present to my grandson in Canada, so I went to the post office.
There was a long line, and I waited for twenty minutes.
The clerk, Ms. Green, was very helpful.
She weighed my parcel on a small scale.
"It's just over two kilograms," she said.
"Would you like to send it by air or by sea?"
By air was faster but more expensive.
His birthday was in ten days, so I chose air mail.
I also bought some stamps and an envelope for a letter to my sister.
Ms. Green gave me a form to fill in for customs, because the parcel was going to another country.
I had to write what was inside and its value.
Nowadays most people send emails and text messages, but I still like the post office.
A letter in an envelope feels more personal.
Is your room full of junk?
Are there piles of clothes on your chair and papers everywhere?
Many people say they feel calmer and more organized when their home is tidy.
Here is how to start.
Do one small area at a time, like a drawer or a bookshelf.
Take everything out and make three piles: keep, give away and throw away.
Be honest with yourself.
If you have not used something for a year, you probably do not need it.
Put things that belong together in containers or boxes.
Keep your school papers in a folder, and put a label on each one.
In the bathroom, keep only the soap and shampoo that you use every day.
The hardest part is not tidying once.
It is staying tidy.
Spend ten minutes every evening putting things back in their place.
Laziness is the enemy, but ten minutes is not much!
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is one of the most famous composers of all time.
He was born in Salzburg, Austria, in 1756.
His father was a musician, and he noticed his son's talent very early.
At the age of three, Mozart could play simple tunes on the piano.
At five, he wrote his first music.
By the age of eight, he had written his first symphony.
His father took him and his sister on long journeys to perform for kings and queens all over Europe.
People were amazed by the little boy who could play the violin and the piano so well.
As an adult, Mozart lived in Vienna and wrote operas, piano music and symphonies.
His music is full of beautiful rhythms and surprising changes.
But his life was not easy.
He often had money problems, and he died when he was only thirty-five.
Today, more than two hundred years later, people around the world still admire his classical music.
Dinosaurs lived on Earth for about 165 million years.
They disappeared about 66 million years ago, long before the first humans.
We know about them because scientists have found their bones and footprints in rocks.
There were many different kinds of dinosaurs.
Some were enormous: they were longer than three buses and weighed more than ten elephants.
They ate only plants.
Others were small and fast, and they hunted other creatures.
Scientists now believe that many dinosaurs had feathers!
Why did the dinosaurs die?
Most scientists think that a huge rock from space hit the Earth.
It caused fires, and dust covered the sky for years.
Without sunlight, plants died, and then the animals had nothing to eat.
But not all dinosaurs disappeared.
Birds are the living relatives of dinosaurs, so their ancestors survived!
In many cities, the best food is not in restaurants but on the street.
Street food is usually cheap, fast and full of flavor.
In Thailand, you can buy spicy curry, grilled chicken and fresh mango with sticky rice at night markets.
In Mexico, people love tacos with meat, onion and hot chili sauce.
In Turkey, a popular snack is grilled meat or fish in bread.
It is often cooked on a barbecue by the sea.
In Vietnam, you can have a bowl of noodle soup or a crispy sandwich for breakfast.
People often eat it on a small plastic chair by the street.
Some people worry that street food is not clean.
It is a good idea to choose busy stalls where the food is cooked in front of you.
If a lot of local people are waiting in line, the food is probably fresh and delicious.
Trying street food is one of the best ways to understand a country's culture.
Artificial intelligence, or AI, is software that can do tasks that usually need human intelligence.
It can recognize faces, translate languages and answer questions.
How does it work?
AI programs learn from huge amounts of examples.
For example, if you show a program millions of photos of cats, it learns what a cat looks like.
Then it can find cats in new photos automatically.
AI is useful in many areas.
Doctors use it to find illnesses in medical images, and banks use it to stop criminals.
Some cars can now operate without a driver in certain situations.
But can machines really think?
Most experts say no, not like people.
AI does not have feelings or imagination, and it can make strange errors.
It is a powerful tool, but it cannot replace human judgment.
We must decide how to use it in a logical and fair way.
The bicycle is one of the simplest and most useful inventions in history.
But the first bicycles looked very different from the bikes we ride today.
In 1817, a German man called Karl Drais built a wooden machine with two wheels.
It had no pedals.
Riders sat on it and pushed the ground with their feet, like children on a balance bike.
Later, inventors added pedals to the front wheel.
Some bikes had an enormous front wheel and a tiny back wheel.
They were fast, but falling off was very dangerous!
In the 1880s, the design improved a lot.
Bikes had two wheels of the same size, a chain and better brakes.
This safe structure is still used today.
The bicycle gave people, especially women, a new kind of freedom.
They could travel on their own, quickly and cheaply.
Today, there are more than a billion bikes in the world, and cycling is becoming popular again in many cities.
Would you know what to do if someone had an accident in front of you?
Here is some basic advice.
First, stay calm, and check that the area is safe for you.
Do not run into a busy road or a building on fire.
Then call the emergency number.
Say clearly where you are and what has happened.
If the person is injured, do not move them unless they are in danger.
Moving them can cause more harm.
Talk to them gently, and ask their name.
If they feel dizzy, help them to sit or lie down.
If there is blood, press a clean cloth firmly on the cut.
Stay with the person until the ambulance arrives.
Your help in the first few minutes can be very important.
Many schools and hospitals offer first aid courses.
It is a good idea to take one.
One day, you might save a life.
Most teenagers spend several hours online every day.
The internet is full of opportunities, but it also has some dangers.
Keep your personal information private.
Do not put your address, your phone number or the name of your school on a public web page.
Use a different password for each account, and never share it, not even with a friend.
Be careful with strangers.
Someone who says they are a teenage girl may really be an adult man.
Never agree to meet someone you only know online without telling your parents.
Think before you post.
A photo or a message can spread very quickly, and it is almost impossible to delete it completely.
Something that seems funny today may be embarrassing in five years.
If someone sends you unkind messages or spreads rumors about you, do not reply.
Save the messages, block the person and tell an adult you trust.
A wedding is one of the most important days in many people's lives.
But every culture has its own traditions.
In many Western countries, the bride wears a long white dress.
After the ceremony, the guests throw rice or flowers at the married couple.
Later, they drink champagne and dance.
In India, brides often wear red, a color of luck, and a wedding can last for three days or more.
Before the wedding, the bride's hands are painted with beautiful patterns.
In Mexico, a long rope of flowers is placed around the couple's shoulders to show that they are joined together.
In Japan, some couples have a traditional ceremony in a temple and then a modern party with a cake.
In Scotland, the groom sometimes wears a kilt.
The customs are different, but the meaning is the same everywhere: two people promise to share their lives.
Many couples celebrate their wedding anniversary every year to remember that special day.
Marta is a sales agent for Sunwise, a company that sells solar panels.
She works for an agency in the city, but she spends most of her time on the road.
Her day starts at eight with a call from her boss.
They talk about her targets for the month.
This month, she has to sell thirty systems.
If she reaches her target, she gets a bonus.
Then she visits customers.
Some are businessmen and businesswomen with large offices.
Others are families who want to save money on electricity.
Marta explains the product and answers their questions.
Her strategy is simple: listen first, then talk.
In the afternoon, she makes a deal with a hotel.
The manager wants panels on the roof.
It is a big trade, and Marta is very pleased.
Back at the office, the secretary helps her with the documents.
At six, she finally goes home.
"It's hard work," she says, "but no two days are the same."
Every year on the fourth of July, Americans celebrate Independence Day.
It is the country's national holiday.
In the 1700s, the thirteen American colonies belonged to Britain.
The British king made the laws and took taxes from the people.
Many people there were angry.
They wanted to make their own political decisions.
In 1775, a war began between the colonies and the royal army.
On July 4, 1776, the leaders of the colonies signed a document.
It said that they were a free nation.
The war continued for several more years.
In the end, the American forces won their independence.
Today, Independence Day is a happy holiday.
There are parades, concerts and barbecues.
People wear red, white and blue.
At night, there are fireworks in almost every town.
For many Americans, it is a day to think about freedom and liberty.
A hundred years ago, many sports were only for men.
People said that women were not strong enough.
Female athletes could not take part in many competitions.
Today, things are very different.
Women play football, rugby, cricket and ice hockey.
They run marathons and climb the highest mountains.
Millions of people watch women's football on TV.
But there are still problems.
In many sports, professional female players earn much less than male players.
A famous footballer who is a man can earn a hundred times more than a woman.
I think this is unfair.
Some people say men's sport makes more money, so the pay is different.
But if women's sport gets more attention and more opportunity, that can change.
Gender should not decide your future in sport.
Your ability should.
School is different in every country.
In Japan, students clean their classrooms every day.
There are no cleaners, so everyone helps.
Most students wear a uniform, even in high school.
In Finland, children start school when they are seven.
They have short days, not much homework and long breaks.
But Finnish students often have excellent results.
In Brazil, many schools have two groups of students.
One group studies in the morning, and the other studies in the afternoon.
In some villages in Kenya, children walk several kilometers to school.
They study with old textbooks, but they are very serious about their schoolwork.
The school year is different, too.
Some countries have two semesters, and others have three terms.
But everywhere, the headteacher gives a speech on the first day!
Almost everyone has a stomachache sometimes.
Usually it is not serious.
Maybe you ate too much, or you ate something too fast.
Spicy or fried food can be harmful for some people.
Worry and stress can make your belly hurt, too.
What can you do?
First, rest and drink some warm water or tea.
Do not drink cola or coffee.
Eat small, simple meals, like rice, toast or soup.
Avoid unhealthy snacks for a day or two.
Some people take a pill from the chemist.
But you should read the instructions carefully.
Doctors advise you to see a doctor if the pain is very strong.
You should also go if it lasts more than two days.
Go immediately if you have a high temperature, or if the pain moves to your chest.
High in the Andes mountains of Peru, there is an ancient city called Machu Picchu.
The Incas built it about six hundred years ago.
The city has temples, houses, stairs and gardens.
They are all made of stone.
The stones fit together perfectly, without any cement.
Even today, engineers admire the structure of the walls.
Earthquakes are common in Peru, but the walls are still standing.
After about a hundred years, the Incas left the city.
Nobody knows exactly why.
For centuries, only local farmers knew about it.
In 1911, an American explorer called Hiram Bingham visited the ruins.
He told the world about them.
Today, Machu Picchu is one of the most famous places in the world.
There is no golden treasure, but the view is wonderful.
There are so many visitors that the government now limits the number of tickets.
They want to protect the city for the future.
Dolphins are among the most intelligent creatures in the sea.
They are not fish.
They are mammals, like us.
They breathe air, so they must come up to the surface.
Dolphins live in groups.
They communicate with each other using clicks and whistles.
Each dolphin has its own whistle, like a name.
Underwater, sound travels far.
Dolphins can hear their friends from several kilometers away.
They are also very good hunters.
Sometimes a group of dolphins swims around a school of fish.
Then they take turns to catch them.
Dolphins do not chew their food.
They swallow fish whole!
People have always loved dolphins.
There are many stories about dolphins helping swimmers.
But today they are in danger from pollution, fishing nets and noise from ships.
We must protect their home.
Dear Editor,
I am writing to express my concern about the new car park on Green Lane.
Green Lane used to be a quiet, peaceful street.
Children played outside, and old people walked safely to the shops.
Since the car park opened in March, everything has changed.
There is heavy traffic all day.
Drivers park illegally on the pavement, and the noise disturbs us at night.
Many neighbors have sent complaints to the city council.
So far, we have not received a response.
This is unfair.
The council should listen to the people who live here.
I would like the council to do three things.
Please put up clear signs, and close the car park at night.
Also, please build a safe crossing for our children.
Yours faithfully,
Tom Walsh
Every summer, my sister and I spend two weeks at our granddad's farm in the countryside.
My granny died a few years ago, so now Granddad lives there alone with his dog, Rory.
Life on the farm is very different from life in the city.
We wake up at six when the birds start to sing.
After breakfast, we help Granddad feed the animals.
Then we collect eggs and pick fruit in the garden.
In August, it is time for the harvest, and we help him bring in the wheat.
It is hard work, and we sweat a lot in the sun.
In the evenings, there is no TV.
Granddad tells us stories about his childhood.
Or we play cards by the fire.
My sister says she is bored sometimes, but I love it.
Granddad says his grandchildren are the best workers on the farm.
I think he says that because he misses us the rest of the year.
Life today is busy.
We work, study, answer messages and look at screens all day.
It is important to find time to relax.
Too much stress can make you ill, and it can cause sleepless nights.
Different people relax in different ways.
Some people like a hot bath with music.
Others go for a walk in the park, or they do yoga.
Many people find that gardening or painting is peaceful.
It gives their mind a rest.
Leisure time with friends is good, too.
Laughing is one of the best ways to relax!
But sometimes it is also nice to be alone and quiet.
Try to turn off your phone for an hour every evening.
Breathe slowly, and notice what is around you.
You may be surprised how much better you feel.
Last Friday, the Circo Luna came to our town.
I went with my little brother, and it was a fantastic evening.
The show started with a clown on a tiny bike.
He fell off again and again.
The children in the audience screamed with laughter.
Then two acrobats flew high above us on ropes.
My brother held my hand the whole time.
My favorite part was the magic show.
A magician made a woman disappear from a box.
Then she appeared again at the back of the tent!
I still do not know how he did it.
There were no wild animals in this circus.
I think that is a good thing.
The performers were talented, and the music was lively.
At the end, the clown gave balloons to all the children.
Tickets are not cheap, but the show is worth every cent.
Where do you prefer to shop: in a big shopping mall or at a local market?
A mall is convenient.
You can find a grocery store, a drugstore, clothes shops and cafés under one roof.
It is warm in winter and cool in summer.
The aisles are wide, and you can use a card to pay everywhere.
There are often special offers, and a shop assistant can help you find what you need.
A market is different.
It is outside, and it can be noisy and crowded.
But the food is often fresher.
It comes from farms near the town.
You can talk to the people who grew it and ask for advice.
Prices are usually inexpensive, and sometimes you can find a real bargain.
I use both.
I go to the mall when I am in a hurry.
I go to the market on Saturday mornings, because I enjoy the atmosphere.
We all write emails, but a good email is not always easy to write.
Here are six simple tips.
First, think about the context.
Who are you writing to, and why?
An email to a friend is very different from an email to a teacher or a manager.
Second, choose an appropriate greeting.
With a friend, you can use a first name: "Hi Anna!"
In a work email, it is more suitable to use a title and a surname: "Dear Ms. Lopez."
Third, mention the reason for your email in the first two lines.
Busy people do not want to read a long story first.
Fourth, be polite.
"Could you send me the schedule, please?" sounds much better than "Send me the schedule."
If you cannot do something, say so kindly: "Unfortunately, I can't come to the meeting."
Fifth, read everything again before you press "Send."
Check the names, the dates and the files.
A missing file means a second email, and nobody likes that.
Finally, if nobody answers after a few days, it is fine to send a short message to remind them.
For nearly four thousand years, the tallest building in the world was the Great Pyramid in Egypt.
Its original height was about 146 meters.
Today it is a little shorter, because it has lost the stones at the top.
Very tall buildings only became possible in the late 1800s.
People started to build with steel, and electric lifts could carry people up and down.
The first skyscrapers appeared in Chicago and New York.
In 1931, the Empire State Building opened with 102 floors.
It remained the tallest building in the world for about forty years.
Today, the record belongs to the Burj Khalifa in Dubai.
It is 828 meters tall, nine times the height of the Statue of Liberty with its base.
Why do cities create such tall buildings?
In a major city, land is very expensive, so it makes sense to build up.
But tall buildings are also a symbol.
They tell the world that a city is rich and modern.
For many visitors, architecture like this is simply fascinating.
Last August, my family had a big reunion at my grandparents' house.
Four generations came together, and our guests were aged from three months to eighty-nine years.
Some of our relatives live overseas, so it was the first time in ten years that we were all in one place.
My grandfather is retired, but he organized everything himself.
He cooked for two days and still had time to fix the garden lights.
My grandmother showed us old photos from her youth.
In one of them, she was a good-looking young woman with long blonde hair.
"That was the year we got married," she said happily.
I met my cousin Rosa from Chile for the first time.
Her face looked familiar, because she looks just like my mother.
In the evening, we all gathered in the garden.
My uncle Leo played the guitar, and everyone sang the old songs.
It was a pity that the weekend was so short.
Before we left, we promised ourselves that we would not wait another ten years.
Rosa's parents want to have the next reunion at their farm in Chile.
I have already started saving for the ticket.
Detective stories are one of the most popular kinds of fiction in the world.
The English writer Agatha Christie wrote sixty-six of them, and people have bought more than two billion copies of her books.
Sherlock Holmes, the detective with the pipe and the strange hat, is another classic.
Most of these stories begin in the same way.
In the first chapter, there is a murder.
The killer is unknown, and everyone in the house has a reason to be afraid.
Then a clever detective arrives and starts to ask strange questions.
Why do readers enjoy this so much?
Part of the answer is that a mystery is a game.
The writer gives us small clues, and we try to find the answer before the detective does.
Everyone seems to be lying.
One character pretends to be ill, and another keeps a gun in his desk.
At first, we blame the gardener; then we change our minds.
Soon we start to doubt everyone.
In the last chapter, the detective sets a trap and finally reveals the truth.
In some stories, the final scene takes place in court, where a clever lawyer asks the questions.
The killer cannot escape, and the world makes sense again.
Perhaps that is the real reason we love these books.
A weather forecast tells us what the weather will probably be like in the next few days.
Scientists use computers, satellites and information from thousands of weather stations to predict it.
Their predictions are quite good for the next three days.
After a week, they are much less certain.
Here is tomorrow's forecast for a town by the sea.
The morning will be cold and windy, with fog near the beach.
The temperature will be roughly five degrees.
Later, clouds will come in from the west, and there is a seventy percent chance of rain.
Thunderstorms are possible in the east in the evening.
What does a seventy percent chance of rain mean?
It means that on ten days like tomorrow, it will rain on about seven of them.
So rain is likely, but it is not certain.
When you read a forecast, look at the wind, too.
A strong wind can make five degrees feel like zero.
If there is a warning about floods, take it seriously.
The weather usually changes gradually, but it can also change very fast.
Chocolate is one of the world's favorite sweet foods, but it starts as a bitter seed.
Cocoa trees grow in hot, wet countries.
Today, most of the world's production comes from West Africa, especially from Ivory Coast and Ghana.
The fruit of the cocoa tree is a large pod, and each pod has thirty to fifty beans inside.
Farmers open the pods by hand.
They cover the raw beans with leaves for about a week, and then they dry them in the sun.
This step gives chocolate much of its flavor.
Next, the dry beans travel to a factory.
There, workers roast them in large batches, like coffee.
The machines break the beans into small pieces and turn them into a thick, dark liquid.
To make a bar, the factory adds sugar, and for milk chocolate it adds milk, too.
Workers test a sample from each batch to check the quality.
So next time you eat a chocolate dessert, think of its long journey.
And think of the farmers, too.
In fact, many of them have never eaten the chocolate that their beans become.
Cities are full of noise: cars, buses, building work, music and people who talk loudly on their phones.
Most of the time, we do not even notice it.
But noise has a strong influence on our health.
People who live near a motorway or an airport often sleep badly.
Even when they do not wake up, their bodies hear the sound.
Their hearts beat faster, and in the morning they feel tired and uneasy.
After many years, this can lead to serious heart problems.
Noise also bothers people at work and at school.
In a noisy classroom, children find it difficult to concentrate.
In a big open office, one loud phone call can disturb twenty people.
Many workers wear headphones, but they feel uncomfortable after a few hours.
What can cities do?
Some have built walls next to their busiest roads.
Others have made quiet lanes where heavy trucks cannot go.
Electric buses help, too, because they move almost silently.
And each of us can help by making less unnecessary noise, especially at night.
Welcome to Pine Valley National Park!
The park is home to bears, wolves, rare birds and more than two hundred kinds of wildflowers.
To keep it safe for everyone, please follow these rules.
Buy your ticket at the entrance, and keep it with your ID at all times.
You can only fish in the lake if you have a license.
Stay on the paths, and never climb over a fence.
It is illegal to feed the animals.
Human food makes them sick, and a hungry bear may bite.
Dogs are welcome, but they must remain close to you.
Fires are forbidden in the forest, except in the special areas near the lake.
You may gather dry wood from the ground, but do not cut any trees.
Please take all your trash home with you.
Even a small plastic bottle can pollute the river for hundreds of years.
The weather in the mountains can change quickly.
Bring warm clothes, water and a phone with a full battery.
If you get lost, stay where you are and call the park rangers.
Behavior that is not acceptable will be reported to the police.
You do not need to be an expert to enjoy the park — just be careful and kind to nature.
Twenty years ago, many people thought that board games were dying.
Children played video games on their PC or phone, and the old games stayed in boxes under the bed.
But in recent years, board games have come back in a big way.
Thousands of new games appear every year, and board game cafés are opening in cities all over the world.
Of course, the idea is not new.
People in Egypt played a game called Senet more than five thousand years ago, and chess comes from India.
So why are board games popular again?
Actually, the reason is simple: people want to spend time together, rather than alone in front of a screen.
Around a table, friends talk, laugh and argue in a friendly way.
Board games are also cheap entertainment, because one game can give you years of fun.
Modern games are very creative.
In some, players build cities or grow farms; in others, they work as a team to save the world.
You need a plan, some creativity and a little luck with the dice.
Other families prefer old favorites like Monopoly, because the familiar rules bring back happy memories.
And quiz games are perfect for parties.
Anyway, whatever you choose, turn off your phone and enjoy the game.
Mai is sixteen, and she is one of the best junior badminton players in the country.
We asked her about her life.
When did you start playing?
When I was six. My father played table tennis, but I preferred badminton.
I got my first racket for my seventh birthday.
What does a normal day look like?
I train for about four hours, two before school and two after.
We don't only hit the shuttlecock. We also run on the track and go to the gym to build strength.
Is it hard to manage school and sport?
Yes, very. I do my homework on the bus, and I go to bed at nine.
There are days when I want to quit, especially after I lose.
But my coach always encourages me. He says that you learn more when you fail than when you win.
What is your biggest ambition?
I want to become a pro and play at the Olympics.
And when I retire, I'd like to open a club for kids.
What advice would you give to young players?
Play because you love it. Take your training seriously, but have fun.
And never stop trying, because effort is more important than luck.
Do you want to play the guitar, speak Spanish or draw faces?
You don't always need a teacher.
Today, there are thousands of free lessons online, so it is easier than ever to teach yourself.
I taught myself to cook this way, and here is what I learned.
Start small.
Many learners fail because they try to do too much in the first week.
Twenty minutes a day is better than three hours on Sunday.
Choose one method and follow it.
You can download a course, use an app or work through a book chapter by chapter.
It does not matter which method you choose, but do not keep changing it.
Expect to make mistakes.
My first cakes were terrible.
But I gradually got better, and every mistake taught me something.
Find other people.
Basically, it is hard to stay interested when you are alone.
Join an online group, share your work and ask questions.
Other learners will encourage you on the days when you want to stop.
Finally, be patient with yourself.
Success depends on practice, not on talent.
If you keep going, you will be surprised by how much you can do in a year.
Most people believe that more money would make them happier.
Is it true?
Scientists have studied this question for many years, and their answer is: partly.
If you are poor, money certainly helps.
It pays for food, a safe home and a doctor when you are ill.
Without these things, it is very hard to feel satisfied with your life.
But once people have enough, extra wealth does not make them much happier.
Even people who win a fortune in the lottery are often no happier a few years later.
So what does make us happy?
A famous study at Harvard University has followed the same group of people for more than eighty years.
Its answer is simple: good relationships.
People with close friends and a loving family live longer and more happily.
The way we spend money matters, too.
Spending on experiences, like a trip with friends, makes us happier than buying things.
Spending money on other people helps, too.
A wise man once said that the best things in life are not things.
Perhaps that is true wisdom.
London is a huge city, but it is easy to get around if you know a few things.
The fastest way to travel is usually the Underground, which Londoners call "the Tube."
It has eleven lines, and in the center of the city a train comes every few minutes.
You do not need a paper ticket.
Just touch your bank card on the yellow reader at the gate when you go in and when you come out.
The system works out the fare for you.
The famous red buses are slower but cheaper, and from the top floor you get a great view.
A bus ride costs less than two pounds, and you can change buses for free within an hour.
Buses do not accept cash, so always carry a card.
At most bus stops, a screen or a timetable shows when the next bus will arrive.
Black cabs are another choice.
Their drivers must pass a very difficult test called "the Knowledge," so they know every street.
But cabs are expensive, especially in heavy traffic.
Finally, remember that cars in Britain drive on the left-hand side of the road.
Before you cross the street, look right first!
At many crossings, the words "LOOK RIGHT" are painted on the ground to help visitors.
The Blue Door is a small family restaurant on River Street.
It opened last spring, and it is already very popular, so book a table before you go.
We visited on a weekday evening.
The room is warm and pleasant, with candles on every table and cloth napkins.
The menu is fairly short, which is usually a good sign.
For a starter, I had the soup of the day, and my friend had a crisp green salad.
Both were fresh and delicious.
For the main course, I chose the steak with boiled potatoes.
It was cooked exactly the way I asked.
My friend had the seafood spaghetti, and she said it was the best she had ever eaten.
We drank mineral water, but there is also a good list of wines and beers.
The only disappointing thing was the service.
The restaurant was full, and there was only one waiter.
We waited forty minutes for dessert, and the people at the next table were getting impatient.
The poor waiter was clearly tired, but he stayed polite and brought us free coffee to say sorry.
Dinner for two cost sixty euros.
Plus, the plates are generous, so nobody leaves hungry.
In my opinion, The Blue Door is worth a visit, but go early or be patient!
What should you wear to a job interview?
The answer depends on the job.
For a position in a bank or a lawyer's office, a dark suit is still the usual choice.
Men often wear a white shirt and a tie.
For a job in a café, a shop or a design company, simple clothes are fine: clean trousers and a nice shirt.
Whatever the job, your clothes must be clean and tidy.
Check your shoes, too, because people notice dirty shoes more than you think.
Leather shoes go well with a suit, and your socks should be dark.
Comb your hair before you go in.
If you wear make-up, keep it natural.
Don't wear too much perfume, because some people dislike strong smells.
Small earrings are fine, and a simple handbag or a bag for your papers is enough.
Why is your appearance so important?
In the first few minutes, the interviewer already decides a lot about you.
Good clothes will not get you the job, but they show that you take it seriously.
Most importantly, wear something comfortable.
When you feel good in your clothes, you feel confident, and confidence impresses people more than any fancy suit.
My grandfather has a small garden behind his house, and it is his favorite place in the world.
He works in it every morning, except when it rains.
In spring, he plants seeds in long, straight lines.
By summer, the garden is full of color.
There are roses, tomatoes, beans and a line of sunflowers that are taller than me.
Birds love the garden, too.
Every morning, a little robin sits on the fence and chirps while Grandpa works.
He says it is waiting for him to find worms.
Grandpa knows a lot about plants.
He taught me that roots need air as well as water, so the ground must not be too wet.
He also taught me to be patient.
"You can't make a flower bloom faster by pulling it," he likes to say.
The garden is not always perfect.
Some years, insects eat half the vegetables.
Once, a storm broke all the tomato plants in one night.
But Grandpa never gets angry.
He just starts again.
When I am in the garden with him, I forget about my phone.
I wander between the flowers, listen to the birds and watch the bees.
It is the most peaceful place I know.
About 400 kilometers above the Earth, a large laboratory flies around our planet.
It is called the International Space Station, or ISS.
It travels at about 28,000 kilometers an hour, so it goes around the Earth about sixteen times a day.
Astronauts have lived on it since the year 2000.
Usually about seven people live there at the same time, and they come from different countries.
Life on the ISS is very different from life on Earth.
There is no gravity, so there is no up or down, and the astronauts float from room to room.
They sleep in bags on the wall, so they do not float away in the night.
Even drinking water and going to the toilet need special training!
Everything that keeps them alive, like air, water and food, comes from Earth or is used again.
The astronauts do not only live there; they work hard.
They do scientific experiments that are impossible on Earth.
For example, they study how plants grow without gravity and how the human body changes in space.
The body gets weaker in space, so they have to exercise for about two hours every day.
The ISS shows that countries can work together.
It also helps us to prepare for longer journeys, perhaps someday to Mars.
Chimpanzees are our closest animal relatives.
About 98 percent of their DNA is the same as ours.
Like human beings, they live in families, they play, and they can feel happy or sad.
A mother looks after her baby for four or five years.
For a long time, people thought that only humans used tools.
Then, in 1960, a young English scientist called Jane Goodall was watching chimpanzees in Tanzania.
She saw one of them push a long piece of grass into a hole.
When it pulled the grass out, it was covered in insects, and the chimpanzee ate them!
What Goodall saw that day changed the way scientists think about animals.
Chimpanzees are clever, but they are also very different from us.
Unlike humans, they cannot speak, although some have learned to use hundreds of hand signs.
They are also much stronger than they look, and they can be dangerous.
Sadly, chimpanzees are now in danger.
In the wild, they only live in the forests of Africa, and those forests are getting smaller every year.
Today there are fewer than 300,000 left.
If we want our cousins to stay alive, we must protect their home.
Long ago, people did not use money.
They exchanged things.
A farmer could give a bag of rice for a pair of shoes.
But what if the shoemaker did not want rice?
So people started to use things that everyone wanted, like salt, cattle or shells.
About 2,600 years ago, in a country that is now part of Turkey, people made the first coins.
Paper money came later, from China, about a thousand years ago.
For centuries, people carried coins and notes in their wallets.
Then banks made life easier, and people started to pay with cheques and later with plastic cards.
In 2002, twelve countries in Europe started to use the same money, the euro.
Today, money is changing again.
In many countries, people hardly use cash at all.
They pay with their phones, and the payment is instant.
With online banking, you can send money almost anywhere in the world in a few seconds.
Some people worry about this.
What happens if the internet stops working?
Others love the convenience and never want to carry a heavy wallet again.
One thing is certain: the way we pay will keep changing.
Fifty years ago, if you loved a song, you had to buy a record.
Records were large, black and easy to break.
In the 1980s, cassette tapes became popular.
They were small, so you could play music in the car or while you walked.
Many teenagers made tapes of their favorite songs for their friends, or for their sweethearts.
Then came the CD, and later the MP3.
Soon people could download a song in seconds.
Today, most people listen on apps.
For a small monthly price, you can hear almost any song in the world.
Styles of music have changed, too.
In the 1970s, disco was on every dance floor.
Rap began on the streets of New York and became a worldwide style in the 1980s and 1990s.
Today, the music charts are full of songs that mix different styles.
Some things have not changed at all.
People still love to sing the lyrics of their favorite songs in the shower.
Superstars still play to thousands of fans every night.
Many young people learn musical instruments from online videos.
And records are popular again, because many listeners love their warm sound.
It seems that in music, old things never really die.
Carla Diaz is a police officer in a busy city.
When she started twenty years ago, people called her a policewoman, but today everyone says "police officer."
Her day begins at seven with a short meeting at the police station.
Then she and her partner get into their car and drive round the city.
Most of her work is not like the films.
She helps people who have lost their way, their wallet or their dog.
She visits schools and talks to children about safety on the road.
And she writes a lot of reports.
But some days are hard.
Last month, two men tried to rob a shop near the station.
One of them was armed with a knife.
Carla and her partner arrived in three minutes and caught them both.
Nobody was hurt.
"The worst part of the job is when people become violent," she says.
"The best part is when you help someone who is in trouble."
Carla believes that a good police officer must be fair and honest.
"Most people are good," she says. "Only a few are dishonest or greedy."
Ben woke up late on the day of his big exam.
His alarm clock was broken.
He jumped out of bed, got dressed in one minute and ran downstairs.
There was no time for breakfast, and he was already hungry and thirsty.
At the bus stop, he waited and waited.
The bus was ten minutes late, and Ben felt more and more impatient.
When it finally came, it was full, so he had to stand.
Then the traffic stopped, and nothing moved for fifteen minutes.
Ben looked at his watch angrily.
He arrived at school at five past nine.
The exam had started five minutes earlier.
He felt confused and a little sick.
"I'm sorry I'm late," he said. "My clock…"
The teacher smiled. "Sit down, Ben. You still have fifty-five minutes."
After the exam, Ben felt uncertain.
A week later, the results came.
He did not get the top mark, but he passed.
It was a little disappointing, but he was not unhappy.
That evening, he bought a new alarm clock.
In fact, he bought two.
His little sister was amused. "Two clocks? You're mad!"
"I'm not mad," said Ben. "I'm careful."
A hundred years ago, school was very different from today.
In many countries, classes were large, with fifty or even sixty schoolchildren in one room.
At the front of the room, there was a big blackboard.
The teacher wrote on it with white chalk, and the children copied everything into their notebooks.
There were no computers, of course, and not many books.
Children often learned long passages from books and repeated them in front of the class.
Teachers were very hard on their students.
If you talked in class or came late, you were in big trouble.
In some schools, teachers even hit children.
Today, this is illegal in most countries.
Many children did not stay at school for long.
They left at twelve or thirteen to work on farms or in factories.
Only a small number of students went on to university and graduated.
Education was mainly for the rich.
Today, school is free in most countries, and many more young people go to university.
Of course, modern schools have their problems, too.
But not many students would want to travel back in time!
Seventy years ago, a television was a big wooden box with a small black-and-white screen.
Most families had only one, and there were only a few channels.
Everyone watched the same programs at the same time.
If you missed an episode of your favorite show, you could not watch it later.
And to change the channel, you had to get up, because there was no remote control!
Today, TV is very different.
Screens are large and thin, and they display beautiful colors.
We can watch shows on our phones, anywhere and at any time.
Instead of waiting a week for the next episode, many people watch a whole series in one weekend.
Some things have not changed.
There are still news programs, cooking shows and quiz shows with popular hosts.
And there are still advertisements, although on some apps you can pay more to avoid them.
Some parents worry that their children spend too many hours in front of screens.
Others say that there has never been so much good television.
What do you think?
On 16 July 1969, a huge rocket left Florida with three American astronauts on board.
Their names were Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins.
They wanted to do something that no one had ever done before: walk on the Moon.
Four days later, Armstrong and Aldrin flew down in a small spacecraft called the Eagle.
Collins waited for them above the Moon.
The landing was not easy.
The computer showed errors, and the Eagle was going toward a field of big rocks.
Armstrong took control and landed it with less than a minute of fuel left.
A few hours later, he stepped onto the Moon, and about 600 million people watched on television.
The two men spent about two and a half hours outside.
They collected rocks, took photos and put up an American flag.
There is no wind on the Moon, so their footprints are probably still there today.
Why was this so important?
At that time, the United States and the Soviet Union both wanted to be first in space.
The Soviets sent the first person into space in 1961.
So the landing was a big success for America.
But for many people around the world, it showed that humans can achieve almost anything.
Since 1972, no one has walked on the Moon, but several countries are now planning to go back.
The Paralympic Games are one of the biggest sports events in the world.
Athletes who cannot see, who have lost a leg or who use a wheelchair take part in more than twenty sports.
The story began in England after the Second World War.
A doctor called Ludwig Guttmann worked at Stoke Mandeville Hospital, where he looked after soldiers who were badly hurt in the war.
Many of them could not walk anymore.
Guttmann believed that sport could make them physically stronger and help them feel better about themselves.
In 1948, on the same day as the opening of the London Olympics, he organized an archery competition for sixteen patients in wheelchairs.
The idea spread quickly.
In 1960, the first Paralympic Games took place in Rome, with 400 athletes from 23 countries.
Today, more than 4,000 athletes take part.
They play wheelchair basketball, run on special legs and swim.
Players who cannot see even play football with a ball that makes a noise.
The Paralympics have changed the way many people think.
Viewers do not see what the athletes cannot do; they see what they can do.
The Games show the importance of hard work and a positive attitude.
Would you like to see a chemical reaction in your own kitchen?
This simple experiment is safe, cheap and a lot of fun.
You need a small plastic bottle, two tablespoons of baking soda, a cup of vinegar, some washing-up liquid and a little red food color.
Put the bottle in the sink, because this is going to make a mess.
First, put the baking soda into the bottle.
Then add a little washing-up liquid and the food color.
Now pour in the vinegar quickly, and step back!
In a second, red foam rushes out of the bottle, like hot rock from a volcano.
What is happening?
Baking soda and vinegar are two different chemicals.
When they meet, they produce a gas called carbon dioxide.
The gas makes thousands of tiny bubbles, and the washing-up liquid holds them together.
This is the same gas that makes some cakes rise in the oven.
A few safety tips.
Do the experiment with an adult, and do not put your face over the bottle.
Vinegar in your eyes is very unpleasant.
If you spill anything, clean it up with water.
When you have finished, you can do it again, as many times as you like!
Every Saturday morning, the square in our small town in England becomes a busy market.
Farmers and shopkeepers put up their tables at seven o'clock.
The fruit table is always the most colorful.
There are red apples, yellow melons, green pears and, in summer, boxes of strawberries.
A melon costs one pound fifty, and a bag of pears costs ninety pence.
Next to the fruit, a woman sells cheese, bread and ham from her farm.
She always lets you try a small piece before you buy.
Around one o'clock, when the market is closing, many things are half-price.
It is a good time to find a bargain, so my brother always waits until then to buy cakes.
In one corner, a van sells hot food.
You can get a cheese omelet or a bowl of soup and a soft drink for five pounds.
There are also stalls with old books, cheap clothes and plants for the garden.
For me, the market is not only about shopping.
It is a place where you chat with your neighbors and meet old friends.
It feels like the heart of the town.
When a button came off my favorite shirt, I wanted to throw it away.
My grandmother was shocked.
"You can fix that in two minutes," she said.
That afternoon, she taught me to sew.
First, you need the right kit: a needle, some thread, a pair of sharp scissors and a few buttons.
Choose thread that is the same color as the shirt, so no one will see it.
Cut about forty centimeters, because long thread gets into a mess.
Push it through the eye of the needle and tie a small knot at the end.
Put the button in the right place.
Push the needle up through the shirt and through one of the holes, then down through the next hole.
Do this five or six times.
Your stitches should be tight, but not too tight.
Finally, tie a knot on the inside of the shirt and cut the thread.
My first button was not perfect, but it stayed on.
Since then, I have learned to repair holes in my socks and even to make a bag from an old pair of jeans.
Sewing is useful, and it saves money.
Besides, it is very relaxing.
Now, when something breaks, I do not throw it away; I sew it.
Most people work in offices, shops, schools or factories.
But some jobs are truly unusual.
Golf players often hit their balls into the lakes on a golf course.
Golf ball divers go down into the cold, dark water and collect them, often thousands in a single day.
The balls are cleaned and sold again.
The job can be dangerous, because the water is dirty and the divers cannot see anything.
In Florida, there are even alligators in some lakes!
Ice cream taster sounds like the perfect job.
Tasters try new flavors and check the quality of every batch.
But they do not swallow the ice cream, or they would eat kilos every day.
One famous taster in the United States had insurance on his tongue for one million dollars.
In London, some people earn money by waiting in a queue for other people.
They wait for hours outside shops when new phones come out, or for tickets to popular shows.
They are paid by the hour, and they need a lot of patience.
Would you like to do any of these jobs?
Many people hate bugs.
Flies land on our food, mosquitoes bite us at night, and fleas make our pets unhappy.
Some insects are indeed harmful.
Mosquitoes carry illnesses that kill more than half a million people every year.
But without insects, our world would be in serious trouble.
Bees and other insects carry pollen from flower to flower.
This helps plants to make fruit and seeds.
About three quarters of the world's food crops need insects in this way, at least in part.
Insects also keep the world clean.
Beetles and flies break down dead plants and animals and turn them into soil.
And they are food for birds, fish and frogs.
Unfortunately, insects are in danger.
Scientists have found a significant fall in insect numbers in many countries.
The biggest reasons are chemicals on farms, the lack of wild places and climate change.
The consequences could be very serious.
We can all help: grow flowers, leave a wild corner in the garden, and think twice before you kill a bug.
When we talk, words are only part of the message.
Our faces, our hands and even our legs communicate, too.
This is called body language.
A smile is the easiest expression to understand, and it means the same thing everywhere.
Other signs are less clear.
If someone crosses their arms, they might be cold, or they might not agree with you.
If someone keeps touching their lips or their chin, they might be nervous or thinking hard.
Tapping your foot often indicates that you are impatient or bored.
Body language can also change from country to country.
In most places, a nod means "yes," but in Bulgaria it can mean "no"!
In some cultures, looking into someone's eyes shows that you are telling the truth.
In others, it can seem rude, especially with older people.
This can easily confuse visitors.
Your tone of voice matters, too.
"That's great" can mean you are happy, or it can mean the opposite if you say it in the wrong tone.
So next time you have an important conversation, do not only listen to the words.
Watch the person, too.
Before the light bulb, people used candles, oil lamps and gas lights at night.
They were dirty, and they often started fires.
Many inventors tried to make an electric light, but their bulbs burned out after a few minutes.
The American inventor Thomas Edison decided to find a solution.
The difficulty was the thin part inside the bulb, called the filament.
It had to get hot enough to shine, but it must not burn.
Edison and his team tested thousands of different things, from paper to hair from a man's beard.
Most attempts failed.
In 1879, they finally made a bulb that worked for more than thirteen hours.
Later, bulbs made with bamboo lasted for more than a thousand hours.
Edison did not invent the first light bulb, but he developed the first one that people could successfully use in their homes.
He also built power stations to bring electricity to whole streets.
Edison believed that every failed attempt taught him something.
Today, we turn on the light without thinking, but every bulb is the result of years of hard work.
In November 1922, a British archaeologist called Howard Carter made one of the most famous discoveries in history.
In the Valley of the Kings in Egypt, he found the tomb of a young king, Tutankhamun.
The king died more than 3,000 years ago, when he was only about nineteen.
Unlike most royal tombs, it was almost complete.
Inside were more than 5,000 objects: gold, furniture, clothes and even food for the king's next life.
The money for the search came from a rich Englishman, Lord Carnarvon.
A few months after the tomb was opened, he became ill and died.
Soon the newspapers were full of stories about a curse.
They said that anyone who entered the tomb would die.
The story frightened people all over the world.
But was there really a curse?
Carnarvon became sick after a mosquito bite on his face.
And Howard Carter, the man who actually opened the tomb, lived for another seventeen years.
Scientists later studied the lives of the people who were there.
They did not die younger than other people.
So the curse was probably just a good story, but people still love it.
Anne of Green Gables is a classic novel by the Canadian writer Lucy Maud Montgomery.
It came out in 1908, and readers of all ages still love it today.
The story takes place on Prince Edward Island, in Canada.
An old brother and sister, Matthew and Marilla, want to adopt a boy to help on their farm.
But by mistake, they get an eleven-year-old orphan girl called Anne Shirley.
Anne has red hair, a playful personality and a huge imagination.
She talks all the time, and she is very frank about her feelings.
Marilla wants to send her back, but slowly Anne wins her heart.
The book is funny and sad at the same time.
Anne makes a lot of mistakes.
She turns her hair green by accident, and she breaks a slate over a boy's head when he calls her "Carrots."
But she learns from her mistakes and grows into a kind, clever young woman.
In my opinion, the best thing about the book is Anne herself.
She reminds us to see the beauty in ordinary things, like trees, flowers and friendship.
If you have never read it, give it a try.
You won't regret it.
The Olympic Games are always changing.
Some sports, like running and swimming, have been part of the Games from the beginning.
But every few years, the organizers add new sports to make the Games more attractive to young people.
At the Tokyo Games in 2021, skateboarding, surfing and sport climbing were part of the Olympics for the first time.
In climbing, athletes go up an indoor wall as fast as they can.
Or they try to finish difficult routes without falling.
In skateboarding, some of the medal winners were only thirteen years old!
At the Paris Games in 2024, breaking, a kind of street dance, joined the list.
Dancers had to win battles against each other while judges watched their moves.
Not everybody likes these changes.
Some people think that dance is an art, not a sport.
Others say that the Olympics must change if they want to stay popular with young people.
For the Los Angeles Games in 2028, there will be even more new sports, including flag football and cricket.
What sport would you like to see at the Olympics?
When it rains in the countryside, most of the water sinks into the ground.
The soil works like a sponge: it holds the water and slowly releases it into rivers and lakes.
In a city, however, the situation is completely different.
Roads, car parks and roofs cover a huge part of the surface, and water cannot pass through them.
So where does the rain go?
In most cities, it flows along the streets into drains, which lead to a network of pipes under the ground.
In older districts, the same pipes often carry both rainwater and waste water from homes.
Normally, all of this water goes to a treatment plant, where it is cleaned before it returns to the river.
The problem comes during heavy storms.
The pipes were built to carry a limited amount of water, and when their capacity is reached, the water has nowhere to go.
Streets turn into rivers, basements flood, and dirty water may flow directly into the river without any treatment.
Because storms are becoming more frequent and more intense, this is happening more often.
Engineers are now looking for solutions.
One approach is to build much bigger pipes, but that is extremely expensive.
Another is to give the water somewhere to go: parks that can flood safely, roofs covered with plants, and roads that let the rain sink through.
In other words, cities are learning to behave a little more like the countryside.
For a long time, people believed that sleep was simply a time when the body and the brain switched off.
We now know that this is far from the truth.
While we sleep, the brain is extremely active, and it goes through a series of stages again and again during the night.
Each cycle lasts approximately ninety minutes.
First comes light sleep, when we can be woken up easily.
Then comes deep sleep, when breathing slows down, the muscles relax and the body repairs itself.
This stage is particularly important for growth and for the recovery of the body after exercise or illness.
Finally, there is REM sleep, which stands for "rapid eye movement."
During this stage, our eyes move quickly behind our eyelids, and most of our dreams take place.
Scientists think that REM sleep helps the brain to process emotions and to store memories.
In one experiment, students who slept well after learning new information remembered far more of it the next day.
What happens if we do not get enough sleep?
After a single bad night, we find it harder to concentrate, and we are more likely to make mistakes.
Over months and years, a lack of sleep increases the risk of serious health problems, including heart disease.
Most adults need between seven and nine hours a night, so sleep is not a waste of time; it is one of the most useful things we do.
In many countries, it is normal for students to have a part-time job.
Some work a few evenings a week in a café or a supermarket; others give private lessons or work in a call center at weekends.
For most of them, the main reason is money.
Rent, food and transport are expensive, and a small extra income can make a big difference.
However, a job can offer much more than a salary.
Students who work learn how to manage their time, deal with customers and take responsibility.
These skills are extremely valuable when they apply for a full-time position after university.
Many employers say that they prefer to hire graduates with some work experience, even if it is not related to their career.
On the other hand, working too many hours can cause problems.
Studies show that students who work more than fifteen or twenty hours a week are more likely to get lower grades.
They have less time to study, they sleep less, and they often feel stressed.
So what is the best approach?
Experts recommend choosing a job with flexible hours, especially during exam periods.
Many universities also offer jobs on campus, such as working in the library, which are designed to fit around lessons.
Before you accept an offer, make sure you know exactly how many hours you will work and whether you can change them.
A good job should support your studies, not replace them.
Today, most of us have dozens of online accounts: email, social media, banking, shopping and more.
Each one contains personal information that criminals would love to steal.
Fortunately, a few simple habits can greatly reduce the risk.
First, use a different password for every account.
If you use the same one everywhere and a single website is attacked, hackers can access all your other accounts, too.
Long passwords made of several random words are both secure and easier to remember than short ones full of symbols.
A password manager, an app that stores them all safely, can also help.
Second, turn on two-step verification wherever it is available.
This means that when you log in, you must also enter a code that is sent to your phone.
Even if someone knows your password, they cannot get in without your device.
Third, update your phone and computer regularly.
Updates often fix security problems that criminals already know about.
Finally, be careful with messages that ask you to click a link or give personal details urgently.
A real bank will never ask for your password in an email.
If you are not sure, contact the company directly using its official website.
Scams are becoming more and more convincing, so a little suspicion is always a good idea.
Most people know the name of their country's president or prime minister, but far fewer know who runs their own town.
